en: Finally!  Tonight, tonight, tonight!  The party is going to be so fabulous.  I shall bed the first man to ask for it.  And the second after that!  I am so sick of these dark, awful times.  Every day is as dreary as the one before.  Well not tonight!  Tonight is for the living!\n\n--Esma
old: 最后！今夜，今夜，今夜！这晚会将会是极好的。我应该和第一个这么要求的男人上床。并且接下来是第二个！我多么渴望这黑暗，可怕的时代。每天都和之前一天一样沉寂。然而不是今夜！今夜是为了活着！\n\n--埃斯玛
new: 最后！今夜，今夜，今夜！这晚会将会是极好的。我应该和第一个这么要求的男人上床。并且接下来是第二个！我多么厌倦这黑暗、可怕的时代。每天都和之前一天一样沉寂。然而不是今夜！今夜属于活着的人！\n\n--埃斯玛
reason: 人工裁决: 原译将“so sick of”反译为“多么渴望”，意思完全相反；末句直译生硬，作最小修正。

en: I am looking forward to the party tonight despite the prospect of so many boorish men talking about their business failures.  What I wouldn't give to meet a fine young musician in this horrible town!  Someone who appreciates the harpsichord for instance and could write me a song.  \n\n--Lydia
old: 今晚我期待着这个宴会，尽管有这么多粗俗的男人在讨论他们生意失败的前景。我怎么就没在这个可怕的城市遇见一个漂亮年轻的音乐家呢！比如一个能懂欣赏羽管键琴且能写为我首歌曲的。 \n\n--莉迪亚
new: 今晚我期待着这个宴会，尽管会有这么多粗俗的男人谈论他们生意上的失败。要是能在这个可怕的城市遇见一位优秀的年轻音乐家，我愿意付出任何代价！比如一个懂得欣赏羽管键琴、还能为我写首歌的人。  \n\n--莉迪亚
reason: 人工裁决: 原译误将“prospect”接入“生意失败”，并将“What I wouldn't give”错解为没能遇见；末句还存在明显病句。

en: Esma's set aside more than enough spirits for the party tonight, I shouldn't wonder.  If she didn't have a drink in her hand she'd positively lose her balance.  Count on me to stay sober, especially in these critical times.  Would that I could escape Dunwall entirely for I have a terrible feeling that someone might be after me.\n\n--Waverly
old: 埃斯玛为了今晚的宴会留出了过多的精力，我不该为此感到惊讶的。如果不是她一只手拿着酒杯，那她肯定会失去平衡的。靠我来保持头脑清醒，尤其是在这个危机的时代。我希望能完全地逃脱顿沃城，因为我有种可怕的感觉，有人可能盯上我了。\n\n--韦弗利
new: 埃斯玛为今晚的宴会留出了多得过头的酒，我一点也不觉得奇怪。要是手里没有酒杯，她肯定连平衡都保持不了。相信我会保持清醒，尤其是在这个危急的时代。真希望我能彻底逃离顿沃，因为我有种可怕的感觉，似乎有人盯上我了。\n\n--韦弗利
reason: 人工裁决: “spirits”在宴会语境中指烈酒，原译为“精力”属于明确错译；并修正由此产生的生硬句式。

en:
Esma Darling,
Here are the three costumes for your party. It pains me that I can't be there, though I'm sure you understand why. I know you're going to look lovely in black. I've enclosed a skeleton key to Dunwall Tower.  When you visit me, no barrier will come between us.

--H.B.
old:
埃斯玛亲爱的，
这是三套为派对准备的服装。即使我确信你一定能理解为什么，我还是为自己不能来十分的难过。我知道你穿着黑色的一定会看上去很可爱的。我已经附上了一个顿沃塔万能钥匙。当你要拜访我的时候，我们之间将不会有障碍的。

--H。B。

--H.B.

en:
Here's the elixir you need to sell on Kaldwin's Bridge this week.
When you've moved everything, bring the money back to the distillery. I'll give you your cut and next week's shipment.
If you're too dumb and you get caught, throw the elixir in the river so that they can't give it to Sokolov. I don't want him figuring out what we're doing. Then throw yourself into the river, too.

--Slackjaw
old:
这是你本周需要的在考德温大桥那卖的药。
当你卖光所有东西的时候，把钱带回酒厂。我会给你你的份还有下周的货。
如果你太糊涂而被抓住了，把药全部丢进河，这样他们就无法将它给索科洛夫。我不想让他弄清楚我们究竟在干嘛。然后把你自己，也丢进河。

--斯拉克·贾尔

en:
As requested, this is a sample of the black market elixir we believe to be coming from one of the abandoned distilleries. No doubt it's inferior to your formula, or even to Piero's Remedy, but people are desperate. We have not been able to identify the additional ingredients. Perhaps you'll have better luck.

One thing of note: Some of the men of the Watch claim, when pressed, to have purchased and used this stuff from time to time since it's cheaper than either of the popular brands. None of them report any illness or complications. So while it may not protect from the plague as well, it doesn't seem harmful.

Lieutenant Christopher Niles
Second Dispensary Detail
Dunwall City Watch
old:
按照要求，这是一个我们相信来自于一个被遗弃的酒厂的黑市灵药样本。毫无疑问，这低于你的标准，甚至是皮耶罗的药，但是人们还是会孤注一掷。我们还无法确认附加的成分，或许你可以。

值得注意的一件事：一些围观的人，当被追问的时候承认，已经不时地购买并使用这种东西，因为这比两种流行品牌都要便宜。他们中没有人回答有疾病或者并发症。因此，尽管它可能无法在瘟疫中保护他们，它看上去也不是有害的。

克里斯托弗·奈尔斯中尉
第二药房详情
顿沃城看守所

en:
26th Day, Month of Wind
I finally found a new place where I should be able to hide and survive for a long time if I stay quiet. The City Watch condemned the building, so this basement should be a safe spot. I have to believe that.

28th Day, Month of Wind
Everything is going as I expected. The Watch patrols in the street nearby, but they never enter this building. Food is the only problem, but I managed to steal some during the night.

2nd Day, Month of Darkness
Someone else found this place and wants to share it. He has a strange amulet made of bone and he claims that it protects him from the plague. We'll see...
Perhaps we can help each other, but I'm losing confidence in the odds of survival.

4th Day, Month of Darkness
Since he arrived, I've been having bad dreams and I don't feel really well.
There're more and more rats in the building.
Soon, I won't be able to leave this shack even if I want to. I'm starting to think that his amulet is cursed.
old:
第二十六天，大风之月
我最终找到了一个新的只要我安静生活就可以让我躲藏并生存许久的地方。城市警卫已经检查过这栋房子，所以这个地下室应该是一个安全的地点。我必须要相信这点。

第二十八天，大风之月
每件事都和我预期的一样。看守在附近的街道巡逻，但他们从不踏进这件房子。食物是唯一的问题，但是我成功地在白天偷窃了一些 。

第二天，黑暗之月
有另一个人找到了这个地方并想和我共享。他有一个奇怪的骨头制成的护身符，他说那可以在瘟疫之中保护他。让我们看看吧。
或许我们可以互帮互助，但我正在失去存活下去的自信。

第四天，黑暗之月
自从他到来后，我一直在做噩梦而且我真的不觉得好。
这房子里有越来越多的老鼠了。
很快，即使我想，我也将无法离开这简陋的房子了。我开始认为他的护身符是个诅咒。

en:
Journal Entry Part Two

6th Day, Month of Rain
My cousin Emil is coming soon, bringing a bird to roast. I'm going to see if any of the shops are still open. Maybe I can buy apples or some potatoes. 

10th Day, Month of Rain
I put my whale bone carving on a shelf, but I could not see it from some parts of the room. So I made a little pedestal for it. It looks nice in the candle light.

15th Day, Month of Rain
Sometimes I dream about it. In the dreams, it makes sounds like the wind, through a broken window. On some nights, the wind sounds like a voice. I was supposed to go to the docks, to ship out, but I remembered too late. It was days ago.
old:
条目日记第二部分

第六天，降雨之月
我侄子埃米尔快回来了，会带来一只烧烤用的小鸟。我会去看看是否还有开着的店铺。或许我可以买些苹果或土豆。

第十天，降雨之月
我把我的鲸鱼骨雕刻在架子上，但是我在房间的某些部分却看不见它。所以我为它制作了一个小的底座。在烛光中它看上去很棒。

第十五天，降雨之月
有时我梦见它。在梦里，它穿过一片破损的窗户，像风一样发出声音。在一些晚上，风的声音像是一种嗓音。我本来是要去码头的，去出货，但是我太晚才记得。那是几天前了。

en:
Journal Entry Part Three

18th Day, Month of Rain
My cousin came, but we fought over it. When I came into the room, he was holding it. I screamed at him and we fought. Now I am filled with remorse. 

26th Day, Month of Rain
He's still sitting in the corner, across from the candles. He was a thief.

2nd Day, Month of Wind
I wonder how he knew about it. Coming to dinner was a trick. 

Maybe he told others. 

7th Day, Month of Wind
Barricades in the halls outside. It is safe now.

11th Day, Month of Wind
The Watch came, taking people away. The neighbors. Someone in the building has the rat plague. Gone now. It promises to protect me. Each night it promises.
old:
条目日记第三部分

第十八天，降雨之月
我侄子到了，但我们却打了起来。当我走进房间的时候，他却掌控着那里。我对他大喊然后我们打了起来。现在我满是悔恨。

第二十六天，降雨之月
他仍然坐在那儿，对面是蜡烛。他是个贼。

第二天，大风之月
我想知道他是怎么知道这个的。来共进晚餐是个骗局。

也许他告诉了别人。

第七天，大风之月
在大厅外的是路障。现在这里是安全的。

第十一天，大风之月
守卫来了，带走了居民，那些邻居。在这栋房子中的一个人患有鼠疫。现在走了。它保证要保护我的。每个晚上它都保证的。

第二十六天，降雨之月
他仍然坐在角落里，对面是蜡烛。他是个贼。

第二天，大风之月
我想知道他是怎么知道它的。来共进晚餐只是个骗局。

也许他告诉了别人。

第七天，大风之月
外面的走廊里设好了路障。现在这里安全了。

第十一天，大风之月
警卫来了，把人带走了。那些邻居。楼里有人得了鼠疫。现在都走了。它答应会保护我。每晚都这样答应。

en:
[Excerpt from the travel journal of a young whaler]

A Gaffer's Tale, Vol 1: Or, A Gaffer's Early Adventures

My sister Nina and I left Tyvia together, saying goodbye to our aunt, the woman who had raised us since childhood. Leaving behind our home city of Yaro and the cold, but beautiful white landscapes we had always known, we boarded a ship for Dunwall. Our parents had left us with a sizable inheritance, and we spent half of this getting to the capital city and establishing a small import shop dedicated to Tyvian furs.

Once I'd helped Nina establish the business, I was free to pursue my dream. Signing on with a whaling ship was the most exciting thing I'd ever done, and I saw it as a means to an end; someday I would captain my own crew, and eventually own a fleet of similar vessels. With tears in her eyes, Nina kissed me farewell and I did not see her again for many months. 

As an apprentice to the gaffer, I got to see the tracking and killing of the great beasts up close. Nothing had ever fired my spirit so, as the wind and pounding waves; racing after a wounded whale, being pulled by a skein of cables embedded in its thick flesh. 

I changed more in those first seven months than I had in the previous seven years. Whaling was beginning to put its mark on me so that Nina barely recognized me when I returned, tanned and sinewy with muscle, weather creases already wrinkling the corners of my eyes. But she could see that I was filled with joy, having found my purpose.
old:
[从一个年轻捕鲸者的旅行日志中摘录]

一个老人的故事，第一卷： 或说，一位老者的早期冒险

在和从童年开始就抚养我们直到长大的姑姑说了再见之后，我妹妹妮娜和我一起离开了提维亚。抛下了我们家乡的薯芋和寒冷，以及我们一直熟知的美丽白色的景观，我们登上了前往顿沃城的船。我们的父母留给了我们一笔可观的遗产，我们花了一半用在前往首都和开一家专门进口提维亚毛皮的小店。

一旦我帮助妮娜建立起生意之后，我就可以自由的追求我的梦想了。和一艘捕鲸船签署协议是我做过的最激动人心的事，我将其视作一种结束的手段;有一天我会拥有我自己的船员，并最终拥有一队类似的船只。在告别时妮娜眼中含着泪吻别了我，我接下来几个月没有再见过她。

作为一个教练的学徒，我近距离看到追踪和杀害大型野兽的过程。没有什么如同风和海浪的冲击一样，曾如此地激发起我的精神;追逐一只受伤的鲸鱼，牵引着一绞嵌在它的厚肉的电缆。

我在这起初的七个月里改变的比我过去七年间的更多。捕鲸在我身上刻上了记号，当我回去的时候妮娜几乎没有认出我，黝黑而有力的肌肉，天气褶皱了我眼框的每个角落。但她能看出来，我是充满了喜悦的，因为找到了我的目标。

捕鲸工头的故事，第一卷：或说，一位捕鲸工头的早期冒险

我妹妹妮娜和我一起离开了提维亚，向从小将我们抚养长大的姑姑道别。离开故乡亚罗和我们熟悉的寒冷而美丽的白色景观后，我们登上了前往顿沃的船。父母给我们留下了一笔可观的遗产，我们花掉其中一半来到首都，开了一家专门进口提维亚毛皮的小店。

帮助妮娜把生意安顿好后，我便可以自由追求自己的梦想。加入一艘捕鲸船是我做过的最令人激动的事，我把它视为实现目标的途径；总有一天，我会指挥自己的船员，并最终拥有一支同样的船队。妮娜含泪吻别了我，之后数月里我都没有再见到她。

作为捕鲸工头的学徒，我得以近距离目睹追踪和杀死巨兽的过程。从没有什么能像狂风和汹涌的海浪那样激起我的豪情；我们追赶受伤的鲸，被嵌入它厚皮里的一束缆绳牵引着前进。

最初七个月里我的变化，比此前七年还要大。捕鲸开始在我身上留下印记；我回来时皮肤黝黑、肌肉精瘦，眼角已经刻上风霜的皱纹，妮娜几乎认不出我来。但她看得出，我因找到了人生目标而满心喜悦。

en:
[Excerpt from the travel journal of a whaler in his final years]
 
A Gaffer's Tale, Vol 2: Or, A Gaffer's Final Passage

After more than a quarter of a century, I am done with whaling, too broken to continue. I've seen all the corners of the Isles and made more coin than most men see in a lifetime. But it's all gone. I've lived through an Emperor and watched his daughter take the throne, fair young Empress she was, but slain so young. Everything beautiful comes to die. I've eaten in every port of the known world and sailed in the loneliest waters you could imagine. I've seen the cliffs around Pandyssia. Even the best of it doesn't give me an ounce of joy. The years come back across my dreams as a line of butchered bodies; long, sleek and singing among the waves under the moonlight, only to be speared by ugly, weather-scarred men who'd knife each other for a good pair of boots. 

Each year I had less time to come home. My tongue forgot the language of small chatter and those who lived in the cities thought me odd. My sister Nina hardly knew what to say to me during our visits. When she lost her business to the Lord Regent's crooked barrister I was a hundred miles east of Morley, gaff-hand frozen from the sleet as we tracked the first bull whale we'd seen in months. I helped her as much as I could, but Nina died in the early days of the plague. None of it mattered. If I'm jaded and bitter, it's because this industry has taken away my dreams. The world has beaten me.

[从一个暮年捕鲸者的旅行日志中摘录]
 
一个老人的故事，第二卷：或说，一位老者的最后遗言

在四分之一个世纪后，我受够捕鲸了，我已经遍体鳞伤，不能继续了。我这一生中已经见过了埃勒斯的每个角落，我挣到的钱比大多数人都多。但是这些都是过去的事了。在我的生命中我目睹了一位国王的女儿继承了王座，那是位善良而年轻的女皇，但她年纪轻轻便遭到谋害。而后每件美丽的事物都消亡了。我在每个港口都吃过饭，在你能想象的到的最偏远的水域航行过，见过环绕着潘迪希恩的高崖。但就算是其中最好的那些事也不能给我带来任何一点的欢愉。那些年像是一条满是遭屠尸体的流水线一般滑到了我的梦里：长长的，干净的梦，在月光的波纹下欢歌。只是它们被那些丑陋的，伤痕累累的人们，那些为了一双好点的靴子就能互捅刀子的人们刺穿了。

年复一年，我回家的时间越来越少。我的舌头都忘记了怎么和人进行聊天，那些住在城里的人都认为我很古怪。我的姐妹妮娜在我们见面时都不知道该说些什么。在她从摄政王手下那个贪赃枉法的大律师那里丢了工作时我正在莫利东方百里之外的海上，雨雪在我们追踪着那只数月来我们见到的第一只巨鲸时把我的鱼叉手冻得很僵。我尽我可能帮助了她，但是妮娜还是在瘟疫开始的那几天就死去了。都无所谓了。如果我消逝了，觉得心里苦涩的话，那都是因为这项工业夺去了我的梦想。这个世界打败了我。

[从一个暮年捕鲸者的旅行日志中摘录]
 
捕鲸工头的故事，第二卷：或说，一位捕鲸工头的最后航程

过了四分之一个多世纪，我不再捕鲸了，身体已经垮掉，再也无法继续。我见遍了群岛的每个角落，赚到的钱比多数人一辈子见过的还多。但如今全没了。我经历过一位皇帝，也目睹他的女儿登上王位；她曾是位美丽而年轻的女皇，却年纪轻轻便遭杀害。一切美好之物终将消亡。我在已知世界的每个港口吃过饭，也航行过你能想象到的最孤寂的水域。我见过潘迪希恩周围的峭壁。即便其中最美好的事，也不能给我带来丝毫快乐。那些岁月在梦中重现，化作一列被屠宰的尸体；它们修长、光滑，在月下的波涛间歌唱，却被一群丑陋而饱经风霜的男人用鱼叉刺穿——这些人能为一双好靴子互捅刀子。

一年年过去，我能回家的时间越来越少。我的舌头忘记了闲聊的语言，住在城里的人都觉得我古怪。每次见面，妹妹妮娜几乎不知道该和我说些什么。她的生意被摄政王手下那个贪赃枉法的大律师夺走时，我正在莫利以东百里之外；我们追踪着数月来见到的第一头公鲸，身为鱼叉手的我被雨夹雪冻得僵硬。我尽己所能帮助她，但妮娜还是死于瘟疫初起的日子。什么都没有意义。如果我已经麻木而苦涩，那是因为这个行业夺走了我的梦想。这个世界打败了我。

[Excerpt from a series of newspaper articles from prominent natural philosophers - By Piero Joplin]

It is through no fault of my own that the average citizen has expressed a preference for Sokolov's Elixir over my own formula, sold as Piero's Remedy, a name I did not choose if you must know the truth. The public has spoken its usual message of idiocy, spending their coin as a means of selecting Sokolov's formula over mine, which I believe to be equal if not superior. 

Much has been made over the popularity of these concoctions as a means of resisting this remarkable new plague. I say remarkable because this strain works with an efficiency we have not seen in the history of the Empire. This plague, now making its way through the City of Dunwall, is unrivaled in its effectiveness. I have studied it within the blood of those so afflicted and it is nearly perfect. Elegant, in fact. 

And while it is true that Piero's Remedy and Sokolov's Elixir are known to protect the body against the plague equally, my own has properties, not fully understood, which relate to the mind itself, and the spirit. And it is in this way that my formula wins out. Here, is where one should pay attention to this contest. For you see, Sokolov's Elixir, with its emphasis on the brute, animal body, is a crass goo better suited for livestock. The subtle and secret variance in the key ingredients making up Piero's Remedy ensure that it works on the higher functions that separate humankind from the mindless blue-jawed hagfish swimming in the Wrenhaven River.

[这一系列文章摘录自突出的自然哲学家 - 皮耶罗·乔普林]

公众对于索洛科夫的而不是我的药剂的偏爱只是我一个人的错误，（索洛科夫药剂）仿照皮耶罗的药剂而这么出售，我并不强求你知道真相。公众们重复着白痴们的话，以此手段达到花费他们的金币在索洛科夫的药剂而不是我的的目的，如果不是我的药剂更好，我相信两种药剂是相等的。

人们已经研究过用这种混合物作为一种流行的对抗这种新的瘟疫的手段。我说，这显著的效率是我们从未在帝国的历史中看到过的。这种瘟疫，正在以它自己的方式，以一种无与伦比的效率穿行在顿沃城中。我已经研究了那些受折磨的人的血液，它几乎是完美的。精致的，事实上。

而且即使众所周知皮耶罗的药剂和索洛科夫的药剂在治疗效果上是一样的，我自己的性质，并未完全理解，那是与自身意志和精神有关联的。且因此我的药剂赢了。这里，关于这场竞争需要值得注意的是。如你所见，索洛科夫的药剂，它强调畜生，动物的身体，是粗鲁的，更适合牲畜。因关键的成分，使得皮耶罗的药剂有微妙的和秘密的变化，确保它能有着更高的功能，区分了人类和有蓝色下巴的在瑞哈文河游的盲鳗。
new:
[摘自知名自然哲学家撰写的一系列报纸文章——皮耶罗·乔普林]

普通市民更偏爱索科洛夫生命药剂而非我的配方，这绝非我的过错。我的配方以“皮耶罗的药剂”之名出售——如果你非要知道真相，这名字并不是我选的。公众一如既往地表明了自己的愚蠢，用花钱的方式选择索科洛夫的配方而不是我的，尽管我相信我的配方即使不胜一筹，至少也与之相当。

这些混合药剂能抵御这种非同寻常的新瘟疫，因此广受欢迎，人们对此谈论颇多。我说它非同寻常，是因为这种病株的效率，是我们在帝国历史上从未见过的。如今席卷顿沃城的这场瘟疫，其效力无可匹敌。我研究过受感染者的血液，它几乎完美。事实上，堪称精妙。

诚然，众所周知，皮耶罗的药剂和索科洛夫生命药剂在保护身体抵御瘟疫方面效果相同；但我的药剂还具有一些尚未被完全理解、与心智和精神本身相关的特性。正因如此，我的配方更胜一筹。这才是这场竞争中真正值得关注的地方。你看，索科洛夫生命药剂强调的是粗野的动物肉体，只是一团更适合牲畜服用的粗劣黏液。组成皮耶罗药剂的关键成分存在微妙而隐秘的差异，确保它能作用于那些将人类与瑞哈文河里游荡的无知蓝颚八目鳗区分开来的高级机能。

[Excerpt from a book on naval history]

While each of the Isles has some form of naval fleet, none is more envied than that of Gristol, with its long, proud history of great ships and the admirals who command them. Boys come of age in the cities of Gristol hoping to someday captain such a ship, and family dynasties are made by those captains who track down infamous pirates or crush seditious uprisings, as during the Morley Insurrection. 

In times of war and peace, Gristol continues to innovate at sea. The ship designs of Anton Sokolov himself now represent the highest standard in the whaling trade, allowing crews to haul their kill up over the deck and begin their butchery and processing, even as the ship returns to Dunwall. The crews can be seen working on their latest whale as the ship moves slowly up the Wrenhaven River, coming to dock with one of the powerful warehouse companies such as the Greaves Whaling House. Suspended in the rigging overhead and backlit by the setting sun, the silhouette of one of these creatures makes a moving site as it cruises to its final resting place in the industrial heart of the capital city.

[从海军历史书中摘录]

虽然每一个岛屿都有某种形式的海军舰队，没有一个比格里斯托的更令人羡慕的，是因为它古老而悠久的强大舰队历史以及对它们发号施令的海军上将。格里斯托的城市中的男孩们成年之际都希望有一天可以掌管这么一艘军舰，在莫利起义期间，家族是由那些追踪臭名昭著的海盗或粉碎煽动起义者阴谋的船长们组成的。

在战争和和平时期，格里斯托一直保持着对于海上方面的创新。安东索科洛夫自己设计的船现在代表着捕鲸业的最高水平，允许船员们在甲板上把鲸鱼杀死，开始他们的屠宰和加工，甚至是在船返回顿沃城的途中。在船慢慢行驶于瑞哈文河上时，可以看到船员们正在对最后一条鲸鱼进行着工作，他们会去一个拥有着强大仓库公司的船坞，比如格里弗斯鲸鱼房。悬浮在头顶的索具和背光的夕阳，这些生物其中一个的轮廓使得这移动的场景正如它游到首都城市的工业中心作为其最后的归宿一样。
new:
[摘自一本海军史书]

虽然每个岛屿都拥有某种形式的海军舰队，却没有哪一支比格里斯托的舰队更令人艳羡；它有着伟大战舰和指挥它们的海军上将所共同铸就的悠久而光荣的历史。格里斯托各城的男孩长大成人时，都盼望有一天能成为这种战舰的船长。那些追捕臭名昭著的海盗，或像莫利叛乱期间那样镇压煽动性起义的船长，更能由此建立起家族王朝。

无论战争还是和平时期，格里斯托始终在海上推陈出新。安东·索科洛夫亲自设计的船只，如今代表着捕鲸业的最高标准；船员能将猎物拖上甲板，在船只返回顿沃的途中便开始屠宰和加工。船只缓缓驶过瑞哈文河时，人们可以看到船员正在处理最新捕获的鲸，随后停靠在格里夫斯鲸油厂之类实力雄厚的仓储公司。巨兽悬挂在头顶的索具上，落日从它身后照来；当船驶向这头巨兽在首都工业核心区的最终归宿时，它的剪影构成了一幅动人的景象。

en:
[Excerpt from a government protocol on disease practices]

Much of the public still harbors false beliefs related to the plague. It is NOT true that the bile from river krusts will protect against contraction of the disease. Nor is it true that crushed Morley orchids act as a remedy, though it is speculated that both of these ingredients are used in both Sokolov's Elixir and Piero's Remedy. Consumption of these products, before exposure to the plague, constitutes the only known means of resisting the disease. 

Further, the Abbey of the Everyman warns against superstitious practices. Not only is it ineffective to burn two hagfish and a cat together, inhaling the vapors while chanting the names of the plague-dead, but it is also considered heresy by the Overseers and will be met with the full measure of the Abbey's laws. 

Tell your neighbors and practice these things yourself: Avoid contact with the infected. Consume your ration of elixir daily, preferably in the morning. And report anyone suspected of carrying the plague. Everyone must work together to stop the spread of the dreaded contagion.
old:
[摘录自政府对疾病的做法协议]

大部分的民众对瘟疫的相关知识依然抱着错误的信念。从河怪那获得的胆汁能治愈鼠疫是不正确的。碎的莫利兰花能作为补救也不是正确的，虽然这两种东西都作为原料被用进了索洛科夫和皮耶罗的药剂。在患上鼠疫前使用这些东西，是目前已知的唯一预防方法。

此外，修道院警告所有人要反对迷信的做法。不仅一边高呼着瘟疫的死难者的名字一边燃烧两种盲鳗和一只猫一起吸入蒸气是无效的，而且这将被监督视为异端，且触碰了修道院全面衡量的法律。

告诉你的邻居而且要自己锻炼以下事情：避免接触被感染者。每日服用药剂，最好是在早晨。并报告任何被怀疑携带瘟疫的人。每个人必须合作来阻止这可怕的传染病的传播。
new:
[摘自政府制定的疾病防治规程]

许多民众仍对瘟疫抱有错误观念。淡水甲贝的胆汁能够防止感染，这并不是真的。捣碎的莫利兰花具有治疗作用，同样不是真的；不过据推测，这两种原料都被用于索科洛夫生命药剂和皮耶罗的药剂。在接触瘟疫之前服用这些产品，是目前唯一已知的抗病手段。

此外，众生修道院警告民众不要从事迷信活动。把两条八目鳗和一只猫放在一起焚烧，一边吸入烟气一边念诵死于瘟疫者的名字，不但毫无效果，也会被督军视为异端，并受到修道院法律最严厉的制裁。

请把这些事项告诉你的邻居，自己也要照做：避免接触感染者。每天服用配给的药剂，最好是在早晨。发现任何疑似携带瘟疫的人都要举报。所有人都必须齐心协力，阻止这种可怕传染病蔓延。
reason: 人工裁决: 当前译文准确区分“防止感染”与“治疗”，并修复了迷信仪式、异端处罚及药剂服用要求等硬错；各组织和物种名称在此均适用。

en:
[Excerpt from a book on sailing traditions and scrimshaw]

Bone charms, a sailor's blessing, they say. 

The carving itself is a practice from long back, passed from father to son, old man salt to greenhorn still getting his sea legs beneath him. In the old times, men cut into the tusks of ice seals and into the arm-long fangs of bears that roamed the isles north of Tyvia.

Once the whale trade began, the practitioners went to engraving the bones of those great beasts, rendering charms that sing in the night and grant some small boon to a man's vigor or defense against pregnancy.
old:
[摘自一本关于航海传统和雕刻的书]

他们说骨头的魅力，是一个水手的祝福。

雕刻本身就是久远的实践，从父亲传给儿子，老手传授新手船上生活时也教这个。在古代，人们在提维亚北方的岛屿上切割冰海豹的獠牙和长臂熊的尖牙。

一旦鲸鱼贸易开始，专职人员雕刻的巨兽的大兽骨，渲染出的魅力会在晚上歌唱且给人一些小小的活力作为恩惠还能避免怀孕。
new:
[摘自一本关于航海传统和鲸骨雕刻的书]

骸骨护符，据说是水手的祝福。

这种雕刻手艺源远流长，由父传子，也由经验丰富的老水手传给尚未适应海上生活的新手。古时候，人们会雕刻冰海豹的长牙，以及游荡在提维亚北方群岛、獠牙长达一臂的熊。

捕鲸贸易兴起后，工匠们转而雕刻那些巨兽的骨头，制成能在夜里歌唱的护符，稍稍增强人的活力，或帮助避免受孕。
reason: 人工裁决: 原译将bone charms反复误作抽象的“魅力”，把arm-long fangs of bears错译成“长臂熊”，且末段句法无法正常传达原意。

en:
[Excerpt from a set of cautionary tales for children]

They say that Jimmy Whitcomb Riley
Was a brawler his mates called Smiley.
He ran around, up and down-town,
Pulling off every kind of crime-y.

On Bottle Street, he hung with the boys,
Throwing bricks and bottles and other toys.
They'd start a fight then run and hide,
Breaking, laughing, far and wide.

Smiley liked to eat and drink all day
And smash and bash the night away.
Drunk and all alone, he drifted off a'sleeping,
Sitting on the bridge along John Clavering.

When he woke, something strange he found,
Stranger than a singing wolfhound.
He'd become a bluejawed hagfish most slimey,
And only remembered his name was Smiley.

They say that Jimmy Whitcomb Riley
Was never seen again for all of time-y.
But he swam around, up and down,
Drinking from the river, crying "why me?"
old:
[摘自一系列的儿童神话故事]

他们说吉米·惠特科姆·赖利
曾经有一个好斗的伙伴叫斯迈利。
他在镇子里上上下下，跑来跑去，
指出每一种犯罪。

在瓶街上，他和男孩们打成一片，
投掷砖块和瓶子和其他玩具。
他们开始一场斗殴然后跑了藏起来，
打破东西，哈哈大笑，渐行渐远。

他喜欢吃吃喝喝一整天。
粉碎和狂欢一整夜。
独自一人醉了，恍恍惚惚睡着了，
沿着约翰·克拉弗林，坐在桥上。

当他醒来，他发现了奇怪的事情，
比一只唱歌的猎狼犬更奇怪。
他变成了怪物，一只蓝色下巴的盲鳗，
只记得他的名字叫做斯迈利。

他们说，吉米·惠特科姆·赖利
再也没有人见过他。
但他游了起来，浮起沉下，
在河中饮水，哭泣着"为什么是我？"
new:
[摘自一系列警诫儿童的故事]

他们说吉米·惠特科姆·赖利，
是个好斗之徒，伙伴都叫他斯迈利。
他在城里上上下下，四处乱跑，
各种罪行都要犯上一遭。

在瓶巷街，他和那帮小子混在一起，
投掷砖块、瓶子和其他玩意。
他们挑起斗殴，然后逃走躲藏，
一路打砸，一路放声大笑。

斯迈利喜欢整天吃吃喝喝，
整个夜晚都在打砸胡闹中度过。
他醉醺醺地独自睡去，
坐在克拉文鹰大道旁的桥上。

醒来以后，他发现了一件怪事，
比会唱歌的猎狼犬还要怪异。
他变成了一条黏糊糊的蓝颚八目鳗，
只记得自己的名字叫斯迈利。

他们说吉米·惠特科姆·赖利，
从此以后再也没人见过他的踪迹。
但他游来游去，时沉时浮，
喝着河水，哭喊着“为什么是我？”
reason: 人工裁决: 原译误解了斯迈利与赖利的关系及多项情节，整体修订必要；当前正确处理瓶巷街、猎狼犬及克拉文鹰大道相关地点，未机械误套普通词。

en:
[Excerpt from a traveler's journal]

Born and raised in Gristol, I spent my formative years in our smaller cities before settling in magnificent Dunwall. There, in the capital city, I learned to appreciate the finer things. When the opportunity arose to document my travels to Serkonos, Tyvia and finally Morley, I left my position as a clerk for the late Lord Estermont. 

Perhaps, like so many in Dunwall, I suffer from being excessively cultured, but I found Morley disappointing. 

Over the course of this journal, I will explain why I found the Festival of Churners to be tiresome, despite the high banners, bare feet, and red robes. And why their renown jellied ox tongue is something I will be struggling to forget for many years to come.
old:
[摘自一位旅行者的日记]

在格里斯托出生长大，我的童年是在我们那的小城镇里度过的，直到我在华美靓丽的顿沃城定居。在这里，在首都，我学习到了去欣赏美好事物。当一个机会出现的时候，我记录下了前往瑟科诺斯，提维亚，最后是莫利的旅行，我离开了为将来成为勋爵的艾斯特蒙特工作的职位。

或许，就像在顿沃城里一样，我受苦于被过度的培养，但是我发现莫利更令人失望。

在这本杂志中，我会解释为什么我发现尽管有着高的旗帜，赤裸的脚，和红色的长袍，搅拌机的节日仍是令人疲惫的。并且为什么他们著名的胶状牛舌是我多年来努力想忘记的。
new:
[摘自一位旅行者的日记]

我在格里斯托出生长大，少年时代生活在这里的小城市里，后来才定居于雄伟壮丽的顿沃。在这座首都里，我学会了欣赏精致美好的事物。后来有机会记录自己前往瑟科诺斯、提维亚，最终抵达莫利的旅程，我便辞去了为已故伊斯蒙勋爵担任文书的职位。

或许我和许多顿沃人一样，受过度教养之累，但莫利确实令我失望。

在这本日记中，我会解释为何那高高的旗帜、赤裸的双脚和红色长袍仍无法让搅乳节摆脱乏味；也会说明为什么他们远近闻名的牛舌冻，将成为我此后多年都难以忘却的东西。
reason: 人工裁决: 原译将“late Lord Estermont”错译为“将来成为勋爵”，将“journal”误作杂志，并有多处明显机翻和语义偏离，故按原文修补。

en:
[Excerpt from a series of letters sent by a member of the Bottle Street Gang]

You want the chinwag on Slackjaw? What he was like when we was young, before he got his name? Oh, he's got a cool head now, but it weren't always like that in the days before he was boss of the Bottle Street gang. Time was, young Slackjaw wasn't such a reasonable man. 

Like most of us, he grew up on the streets, running with a pack of ragamuffins and avoiding the law, pinchin' whatever he needed. Dark haired and dark eyed, smokin' a pipe by the age o' ten. For them born into the brothels or coming from the orphanages, it was either the gangs or workin' with the mud larks and no one wants that. Some got pressed into the Navy or put down in the mines run by the Pendleton or Boyle families. As hard as it was on the streets, as hungry as we all got, at least we was free. 

By the time we weren't little 'uns any more, Slackjaw was one to watch, usually callin' the shots when we took down a farmer's cart or sidewalk street vendor. He'd come up with the plan, give everyone some part to play and decide on the split. Most of us just went along, 'cause we learned fast that we made out better like that. More food, more coin. Plus, none of us wanted to deal with Slackjaw when he was in a rage. 

He worked on a couple of big jobs with Black Sally across town, and that was enough to get the attention of the other bosses. He wasn't just a street kid any more. Now he was an up-and-comer, which meant trouble. 

Another guy who fancied himself as such was Mike the Fish, who was workin' his way up running the protection racket among the factory women. One fine evening we're all taking in a bawdy show in the theater house. Mike the Fish and his lot are there in the cheap seats too, just down the aisle from us. Mike gets a wild idea - he wasn't big on planning - and throws a heavy ceramic spittoon at Slackjaw. Hits him square in the face and breaks his jaw. We look to see if there's gonna be a blood brawl, but Slackjaw just points at the door and we all leave, with Mike laughing at our backs. 

Waking up the next day, without telling us why, Slackjaw motions for us all to follow. He still can't say a word, so we just come along. We stop at the docks and Slackjaw buys - actually pays coin for it - a heavy chain covered in hooks. It's for fishing in the deep, something you'd attach to a long line off the side of a ship. It's about four feet, made of thick links, and there are shark hooks comin' off it at different angles. Slackjaw's got that thing wrapped around his left arm, danglin' at his side. 

Not sure how he knew where Mike the Fish was stayin', but when we reach his girl's house, Slackjaw throws a bottle through the window just like that. It's almost noon. There's a bunch of screamin' inside and Mike pokes his head out, looking wide-eyed and baffled. When he sees Slackjaw out in the street, a look comes over his face that still gives me the willies. Pure murder. 

Mike comes out the side door bellowin' like a bloodox, holding a cleaver, heading straight for Slackjaw. When they come together in the street, Slackjaw spins and the shark hooks bite deep into Mike's arm and shoulder. He screams, but Slackjaw holds onto the chain. He's standin' there with his jaw broken, clenched tight, with the chain wrapped around his left arm, hooks sunk into Mike the Fish, just knifing him as fast as he can. Mike couldn't fight very well, hooked like that and using his left hand, but he was a big guy and it took a lot of stabbin' before he went to his knees. Everyone was cheering at first, but then we all went quiet. It just kept goin' and goin', until finally it was just Mike the Fish blubberin', cryin' like a baby, and the sound of Slackjaw's knife. 

When it was over - and here's the brilliant part - Slackjaw took out a note and stuck to Mike's face with a nail. It just said, If you want a job, come to Bottle Street. 

Slackjaw didn't talk right for a couple of months, but word spread fast. 

By the end of the year, once we had a sizable gang goin', he sent out letters to the other bosses, tellin' them that he was running a brand new crew over on Bottle Street. Most of them laughed or beat up the guys who delivered the letters. Green-eye Trish even came back missing a thumb. But apparently Slackjaw was expecting that kind of reaction and had a backup plan. 

A week later, four of the bosses were dead. Seemed like a series of unfortunate events, but everyone knew better. One shot dead by the Watch while standing in the middle of a meat market. Another slipping and falling into the water, out cold. One of the older bosses found in bed with his belly opened wide and a Tyvian pear stuffed into his mouth. Still not sure what that meant. And Sheila Barnsworth was found bubblin' in a cauldron o' hot wax.

Slackjaw sent out another set of letters. Offers to the under-bosses, telling 'em they'd be treated fair as peers. He even sent Green-eye Trish with one of the letters. All of the under-bosses accepted. 

After spilling the guts of his main competition, Slackjaw went in for stabilizin' his business, real neat like. Calling in favors, smoothing things over, giving everyone a little bit of coin or drink as a bonus. Showin' what he could be like as boss. So everything got quiet, which always makes the boys of the City Watch nervous, of course. 

Word went out among the Royal Spymaster's snitches, the Responsible Citizens Group they called themselves, telling everyone working in a shop or sweeping off the front steps of their homes to keep watchful eyes for Slackjaw and his men. Tryin' to suss out what they were up to and what had just happened. But Slackjaw aint stupid. He greased a few palms among the shopkeepers and the Watch too, telling them that he was in town to stay and that things would be run properly from now on, without so much blood. He was finally a real boss, ready to settle into the business of moving whiskey, running the hound fights, and offering up the ladies and gentlemen of the night if you take my meaning. 

Then the plague came. 

At first it seemed like a good thing. A few people got sick and everyone wanted to buy those potions, from Sokolov or Piero. Health elixir or spiritual remedy they call 'em. Slackjaw told me he saw an opportunity. We already had an old whiskey factory with a still, where we could water the stuff down and sell it discounted. Doing the same with with Sokolov's elixir was a smart plan. Pretty soon everybody in the slums was sick and business was good. But after a while there were so many people down with plague that everyone got scared. Everybody started actin' real nasty and everything fell apart. When people can't work, they don't have the coin for elixir, watered down or pure. 

When the Empress died, it seemed like Dunwall would slide into the Void. Spymaster Burrows took over and the Watch started using all that new Sokolov technology. Watchtowers, tallboys and them arc pylons. They put up a wall of light across Clavering Boulevard and cracked down hard. 

But Slackjaw surprised us again. Instead of leaving town on a boat bound for Morley or one of the other Isles, he stayed and kept it all together. We get as much elixir to fight off the plague as the City Watch, with their taxes and rations. And that's kept us alive, so far. 

--Crowley, Bottle Street Gang
old:
[摘自一系列的瓶街帮成员寄来的信件]

你想和大嘴巴聊聊天？当我们还年轻时，在他得到这个名字之前，他是怎样的一个人？噢，他现在有冷静的头脑，但是在他成为瓶街帮成员的老板之前并不是这样子的。曾有一个时候，年轻的大嘴巴不是这么一个公道的人。

就像我们中的大部分人一样，他在街头长大，和一帮衣衫褴褛的人一起游走，无视法律地拿走一切他所需的。深色的头发和眼睛，十岁就开始抽烟。因为他们生在到妓院或来自孤儿院，不是成为帮派成员工作就是一大早起床去泥泞的地方工作，没人喜欢这样。一些人在由潘多顿或者波义耳家族运营的海军或是矿山那儿备受压力。就和在街道里一样的艰难，和我们感受到的一样饥饿，至少我们是自由的。

在我们不是小孩子的时候，在我们抢夺农夫的运货马车或街头小贩的东西时，通常都是大嘴巴来发号施令。 他会想出计划，让每个人分工合作，各司其责。我们大多数人只需照做即可，因为这样我们可以很快上手并且收获也更丰富。食物越多，钱越多。还有，大嘴巴发怒的时候，我们没人敢去招惹他。

他在镇子里，和黑萨利一起忙着几个重要的活儿。这足以引起其他大佬的注意了。他现在可不再是街头的小混混了，作为一个后起之秀，这也意味的麻烦来了。

另外一个叫做游鱼迈克家伙把自己当成大嘴巴那样的人物，他的营生就是对女工收取保护费。在一个美好的夜晚，我们全都在剧院里面看艳舞。游鱼迈克和他的小弟们也在那里，他们坐在低等座上，就在走廊那边。迈克有了个疯狂的念头 - 他一向想不出什么好点子 - 他朝大嘴巴扔了个挺重的瓷痰盂。直接砸在了他脸上，把他的下巴都砸碎了。我们寻思着接下来估计会有一场血斗，结果大嘴巴只是指着门，然后我们就都走了，留下迈克一个人在我们后边大笑。

第二天，大嘴巴什么也没说，就让我们跟着他。大嘴巴买了根 - 确实是付了钱的 - 满是鱼钩的链子，还挺沉的。这东西是用来钓深海鱼的，可以把它沿着船边，挂很长一条。大概有四英尺长吧，是用很厚实的链环结成的，各个角度都挂有鲨鱼钩。大嘴巴把这玩意缠在左臂上，垂在一边。

不知道他是怎么知道游鱼迈克在哪里的，反正我们到了他女人的房子的时候，大嘴巴隔着窗户，朝他扔了个瓶子。那时候差不多是中午了。只听得屋里传出一阵尖叫，然后迈克探出头来，瞪着眼睛，一脸困惑。当他看到大嘴巴在街上的时候，那表情至今仍让我毛骨悚然。完全就是张杀人犯的脸。

迈克从侧门冲出来，像头浑身鲜血的公牛一样怒吼着，抄着把砍刀，直奔大嘴巴。他们在街上刚一对上，大嘴巴就旋转着甩出鲨鱼钩，深深地钩进了迈克的胳膊和肩膀。他大叫着，但是大嘴巴紧握着链子。他牢牢地抓着缠在左臂的链子，拖着个被打破了的下巴站在那里，鱼钩深深地没入了游鱼迈克的身体，他以最快的速度划开迈克的皮肉。迈克被钩成那样，只好用左手，根本没法打了。但他身躯庞大，费了好大的劲儿，才让他在大嘴巴的脚边停下来。大家一开始都在欢呼，但是后来都噤声了。大嘴巴还在不停地折磨他，最后只剩下迈克哭爹喊娘和皮开肉绽的声音。

最妙的就是完事之后，大嘴巴在迈克脸上钉了张纸条。上面写着：如果你想找工作，就来瓶巷街。

大嘴巴好几个月都没说话，不过名气一下子就传开了。

年末的时候，我们帮派就发展得相当壮大了。他派人给其他帮派头目传信，告诉他们自己在瓶巷街组建了一个新的帮派。其他大部分帮派都嘲笑我们，有的还殴打传信人。绿眼崔什甚至少了个拇指。但显然，这些都在大嘴巴预料之中，而且他还有后招。

一周之后，死了四个头目。看起来就像是一些意外事件一样，但大家都知道发生了什么。有个头目在肉市被警卫射杀，还有一个滑落水中被淹死。年长的那个头目则死在自己床上，被开膛破肚，嘴里还塞了个提维亚梨。没人知道是什么意思。而希拉·巴恩斯沃思的尸体在装满热蜡的大锅中冒着泡。

大嘴巴又派人去传信。告知那些帮派的二把手们，他们会得到同等待遇。他甚至还让绿眼崔什也出去送信。所有的二把手都接受了大嘴巴的条件。

在他的主要竞争对手都吓破胆以后，大嘴巴开始着手他的生意，都是些看起来挺干净的生意。招人帮忙，息事宁人，施以小恩小惠。他展现了一个头目该有的样子。所以一切都变得很平静了，这反而让城市警卫那帮小屁孩紧张得很。

事情很快在皇家间谍大师的线人中传开了，这些人自称为市民职责小组。他们告知别人，不管在干什么，都要盯着大嘴巴他们。他们想弄清楚这个帮派的一切动向。大嘴巴可不蠢，他也买通了一些店主和警卫，还告诉他们自己会待在镇子里，从此以后，所有事情都会顺利如常，不会有那么多的流血冲突了。最后，他终于成了真正的头目，掌控着威士忌的运输，经营斗狗赛事，还给女士和先生们提供一夜风流。

接着，瘟疫来了。

一开始还像是好事。少数人得了病之后，所有人都想要买索科洛夫或者皮耶罗的药。他们把这些东西叫做灵丹或者妙药。大嘴巴告诉我，他看到了机会。我们已经有了个带蒸馏室的旧威士忌酒厂，以前在那里把酒稀释了再拿出去卖。现在我们也能照搬此法，去卖索科洛夫的药。很快，贫民区的人都病了，生意非常火爆。但是没多久，很多人都死于瘟疫，大家都害怕了。接着就是暴乱，一切都分崩离析了。因为人们不能工作的话，不管是稀释的药还是纯品，他们都没钱买。

女皇一死，顿沃城看起来也像是要完蛋了。间谍大师巴罗斯独揽大权，警卫开始使用索科洛夫所有的新技术。瞭望塔，高脚机器人还有电弧塔。他们建造了一座横亘克莱文鹰大街防御工事，开始无情地镇压。

而大嘴巴再一次地让我们吃惊了。他没有坐上去往莫利或者其他岛屿的船，而是选择留下稳定事态。我们给城市警卫提供药剂，换取他们来收税，配给物资。这才击退了瘟疫，让我们活到了现在。

-- 克劳利，瓶街帮
new:
[摘自一系列由瓶街帮成员寄出的信件]

你想听听大嘴巴的闲话？想知道我们年轻时、他得到这个名字之前是什么样？哦，他现在头脑冷静，可在成为瓶街帮老大以前并非一直如此。曾经，年轻的大嘴巴可不是个讲道理的人。

和我们大多数人一样，他在街头长大，跟一群衣衫褴褛的小鬼厮混，躲避法律，缺什么就偷什么。他黑头发、黑眼睛，十岁就抽起了烟斗。那些生在妓院里或从孤儿院出来的孩子，不是加入帮派，就是去和拾泥童一起干活，没人愿意选后者。有些人被强征入海军，或被送进潘德顿家族或波义耳家族经营的矿井。街头生活再苦，我们再饿，至少还是自由的。

等我们不再是小孩子时，大嘴巴已经成了不可小看的人。我们劫农夫的货车或街边小贩时，通常都由他发号施令。他负责想计划，给每个人安排差事，再决定如何分赃。我们大多照他说的做，因为很快便发现这样收获更多：更多食物，更多钱币。况且，大嘴巴发怒时，没人愿意招惹他。

他和城另一头的黑萨利合作干过几桩大买卖，足以引起其他头目的注意。他不再只是街头小子，而成了崭露头角的人物，这也意味着麻烦。

另一个自认也是这种人物的家伙叫游鱼迈克，他靠向工厂女工收保护费一步步往上爬。一天晚上，我们全都在剧院看艳俗表演。游鱼迈克和他的手下也坐在廉价席上，就在过道另一边。迈克突然冒出个疯狂念头——他向来不擅长谋划——抄起一个沉重的陶瓷痰盂砸向大嘴巴。痰盂正中面门，打断了他的下巴。我们都等着看一场血战，大嘴巴却只是指了指门，于是我们全都离开了，任由迈克在身后嘲笑。

第二天醒来后，大嘴巴没有解释原因，只示意我们跟上。他的下巴还让他说不出话，我们便一路随行。到了码头，大嘴巴买下——真掏钱买下——一条布满钩子的沉重铁链。这东西用于深海捕鱼，要接在船舷垂下的长索上。铁链约四英尺长，链环粗重，各个方向伸出鲨鱼钩。大嘴巴把它缠在左臂上，垂在身侧。

不知道他怎么查到游鱼迈克住在哪里。我们来到迈克女人的住处后，大嘴巴二话不说便把一只瓶子砸进窗户。当时快到正午，屋里传来一阵尖叫，迈克探出头来，瞪大眼睛，一脸困惑。他看到站在街上的大嘴巴时，脸上浮现出的神情至今仍让我不寒而栗：纯粹的杀意。

迈克像头血牛般咆哮着从侧门冲出，手持砍刀直奔大嘴巴。两人在街上交锋时，大嘴巴猛然旋身，鲨鱼钩深深咬进迈克的手臂和肩膀。迈克放声惨叫，大嘴巴却紧抓铁链不放。他就那样紧咬着断裂的下巴站在那里，铁链缠在左臂，钩子陷进游鱼迈克的身体，同时用刀飞快地一下下捅他。迈克被钩住后只能使用左手，根本无法好好还击；但他块头很大，大嘴巴刺了许多刀，他才跪倒在地。起初所有人都在欢呼，后来却全都沉默了。那场面没完没了，最后只剩游鱼迈克像婴儿般抽泣的声音，以及大嘴巴一刀刀落下的声音。

结束之后——最精彩的部分来了——大嘴巴取出一张纸条，用钉子把它钉在迈克脸上。上面只写着：想找活干，就来瓶巷街。

大嘴巴有几个月都没能正常说话，但消息很快传开了。

到了年末，我们已经拉起一支规模不小的帮派。他给其他头目寄出信件，告诉他们自己正在瓶巷街经营一支全新的队伍。大多数人不是嘲笑他，就是殴打送信的人。绿眼崔什回来时甚至少了一根拇指。但大嘴巴显然早料到会有这种反应，也准备了后手。

一周后，四名头目死了。看起来像一连串不幸事故，但人人都心知肚明。一个站在肉市中央时被城市警卫开枪打死；另一个失足落水，当时已经不省人事；一名年长头目被发现死在床上，肚子被剖开，嘴里塞着一只提维亚梨，我到现在也不知道那是什么意思；希拉·巴恩斯沃思则被发现浸在一锅热蜡里冒泡。

大嘴巴又寄出一批信件。这次是给二把手们的提议，承诺将他们当作平等的伙伴公平对待。他甚至又让绿眼崔什送去一封。所有二把手都接受了。

除掉主要竞争对手后，大嘴巴开始稳固生意，手法非常利落。他收回人情、平息纠纷，还给每个人一点钱币或酒作为奖赏，让大家看看他当老大时会是什么样。于是局面安静下来，而这种安静自然总会让城市警卫紧张。

皇家情报部长的密探——那群自称“尽责公民团”的人——传出消息，要所有在店里工作或清扫自家门阶的人都盯紧大嘴巴及其手下，查清他们在做什么，以及此前究竟发生了什么。但大嘴巴并不蠢。他买通了几个店主，也打点了城市警卫，告诉他们自己会在城里扎根，从此一切都会有规矩，不再流那么多血。他终于成了真正的老大，准备安稳经营威士忌运输、斗狗，以及——你懂我的意思——为人提供夜间的女士和先生。

然后瘟疫来了。

起初，这似乎是件好事。几个人染病后，人人都想购买索科洛夫或皮耶罗的药剂，也就是所谓的索科洛夫生命药剂和皮耶罗精神药剂。大嘴巴告诉我，他看到了商机。我们本来就有一座带蒸馏器的旧威士忌酒厂，可以在那里给药剂兑水，再打折出售。用同样的方法处理索科洛夫生命药剂是个聪明计划。很快贫民区人人患病，生意兴隆。但后来感染瘟疫的人实在太多，所有人都害怕起来。大家开始变得凶恶，一切随之分崩离析。人们无法工作，就没有钱购买药剂，无论兑过水还是纯的都一样。

女皇死后，顿沃仿佛将要沉入虚空。情报部长巴罗斯掌权，城市警卫开始使用索科洛夫的各种新技术：瞭望塔、高跷小子和电弧塔。他们在克拉文鹰大道架起光之壁，开始严厉镇压。

但大嘴巴又一次令我们吃惊。他没有乘船逃往莫利或其他岛屿，而是留下来维持住了一切。我们获得的抗疫药剂和城市警卫一样多，尽管他们有税收和配给。正因如此，我们才活到了现在。

--克劳利，瓶街帮

en:
[Excerpt from the personal memoirs of Hiram Burrows, dated several years earlier]

This is the Fourth Day, Month of High Cold. 

Progress continues on the suppression of gang activity in the Distillery District, but more slowly than I'd expected. The ruffians operating there have been cunning, I'll grant them that, but it's only a matter of time. I'll see their leaders flogged in public and sent beneath the Royal Executioner's blade. If I had my way, that mute bastard would be working night and day, removing the heads that need removing.  

Internally, the Empress does not seem pleased with my investigations. It seems that it is beyond her thinking - against her very nature as a trusting person - to believe that traitors move among us, but I know they do. They must. 

No, Jessamine would rather spend her time with the Royal Protector. At least he's likely to stop any immediate threat to her safety, but a strong arm is not what's needed against those who would undermine us. How will Corvo's sword stop a poisoned wine glass or an explosive delivered by courier? It will not. There are many threats around us. Threats requiring meticulous efforts to police. 

Young Lady Emily is undisciplined, I'm afraid. Here within Dunwall Tower, she receives instruction from the finest tutors known in the Isles, yet her mother spoils her and she spends most of her time lost in imagination, wasting her time drawing, or asking Corvo to teach her to fight with wooden sticks. The girl might rule the Empire some day; every moment spent at play is a moment wasted. 

Shoring up security for the main gate leading into Dunwall Tower has been another pet project of late. To think that back in his day Emperor Kaldwin left it open to the public during the day, allowing anyone to come and go as they pleased. If it were up to me, I'd seal off access to the streets entirely, but the Empress won't hear of it. The water lock is much easier to protect and if it were the only way in to the Tower, traffic in and out would be greatly reduced. Someday the wrong person is going to slip in and we'll suffer for it, mark my words. No amount of security is excessive when it comes to protecting heads of state. 

The Empress also disapproves of my plans for the Sokolov devices. Sokolov himself has no interest in security, of course, but he's vain and therefore keen to see his inventions deployed in any fashion. This "wall of light" he's been tinkering with has promise. In any case, at least I was able to convince the Empress to upgrade the pistols carried by the officers of the Watch. 

Why do I worry so, when no one else seems to care? If I ever fall asleep, will it all sink into the Ocean? Will the rough things clamber over the walls and fill themselves on our flesh? This is what I see in the same dream several times each month. If only I had more say in things, more authority, I could protect us all.

Perhaps I have been working too hard. Dinner and an evening of conversation with a certain lady of refinement might be in order, perhaps somewhere nice in the Estate District. 

--Hiram Burrows, Royal Spymaster
old:
[从希拉姆的洞穴的个人回忆录节选，记录于几年前]

这是第四天，寒冷之月。

对酿酒区的帮派活动的抑制进程正在继续，但是比我预想的要慢。歹徒们很狡猾，我会搞定他们，但这只是一个时间问题。我会看到他们的领导人在公共场合被打并被送到皇家刽子手的刀下。如果我有我的方式的话，这安静的混蛋会被派去日夜地工作，然后砍掉必须要砍掉的头。 

真心的说，女皇显得并不怎么对我的调查满意。似乎这是超乎她的想法的-这是不符合她那作为一个轻信的人的天性的-来相信我们之间有叛徒，但我知道他们是这样的。他们一定是的。

不，贾斯敏宁可花时间和皇家护卫在一起。至少他看上去是会立刻阻止任何对她安全的威胁的，但是一个强有力的手臂并不是我们在面对想要暗中破坏我们的人的时候所需的。科尔沃的剑该如何停下下毒的酒杯或是会爆炸的邮递呢？它不行的。我们身边存在着许多的威胁。这些威胁需要警方细致的努力。

我恐怕，年轻的艾米莉女士是训练不足的。在顿沃塔内，她在受到群岛最优秀导师的指导，然而，她的母亲溺爱她，她大部分的时间都花费在想象之中，或是叫科尔沃用棍子教她如何战斗。这女孩或许会某天统治这个帝国; 把每刻都花在游玩上只一种对时间的浪费。

加强顿沃塔的主要入口的安全成为了过晚的另一个项目。回想当年考德温帝王把顿沃塔在白天开放给民众的日子，允许任何人如其所愿地进来离开。如果这是由我决定的，我会完全关闭去往街道的入口，但是帝王不会听从这个的。用水门锁来保护是更容易的事而且这是唯一的进入高塔的方法，进出的交通将会急剧地减少。要记住我的话，有一天错误的人会偷偷溜进去，于是我们就会遭殃。谈到对于国家头脑的保护再多的安全措施都不嫌多。

女皇还拒绝了我用索洛科夫武器武装的计划。索洛科夫自己对于防卫安全也没什么兴趣，当然，但是他自负如此，因此渴望看到他的发明部署在任何时尚的地方。这个“光之墙” 他一直承诺过的在摆弄着。无论如何，至少我能够说服女皇升级城市警卫官携带的手枪。

当其他人都不看上去在意的时候，我为什么这么担心？如果我睡着的时候，会不会一切都沉入大海之中呢？会不会有粗野的东西翻阅过墙壁然后用我们的肉体来充实自己呢？这就是我每个月要梦见几次的东西。如果我更多的话语权，更多的权力，我可以保护我们所有人。

或许我工作得太努力了。一顿晚餐及晚上和一位优雅的某位女士的畅谈或许是正确的，或许会在某个地产区的好地方。

--海罗姆·巴罗斯，皇家间谍长
new:
[摘自希拉姆·巴罗斯数年前的个人回忆录]

今日是严寒之月第四日。

镇压酿酒区帮派活动的行动仍在继续，但进展比我预想的缓慢。盘踞当地的暴徒确实狡猾，这一点我承认，但解决他们只是时间问题。我会亲眼看着他们的头目遭到公开鞭打，再被送到皇家刽子手的刀下。若能由我做主，那个哑巴混蛋就得日夜不停地工作，砍掉所有该砍的脑袋。

私下里，女皇似乎对我的调查并不满意。她生性信任他人，要她相信我们中间有叛徒活动，似乎超出了她的理解，也违背了她的天性。但我知道叛徒确实存在。他们必然存在。

不，贾斯敏宁愿把时间花在皇家护卫身上。至少他大概能阻止任何迫在眉睫的安全威胁，但面对企图从内部破坏我们的人，光靠强壮的手臂毫无用处。科尔沃的剑如何阻止一杯毒酒，或一件由信使送来的爆炸物？它做不到。我们周围危机四伏，必须以一丝不苟的警务工作加以防范。

恐怕艾米莉小姐缺乏管教。在顿沃高塔内，她接受群岛最优秀导师的教导，可她的母亲宠坏了她。她大部分时间都沉浸在幻想中，不是浪费时间画画，就是缠着科尔沃教她用木棍战斗。这个女孩将来或许会统治帝国；每一刻玩耍的时间都是浪费。

近来另一项由我特别推动的计划，是加强顿沃高塔正门的安全。想想考德温皇帝在位时，白天竟会将大门向公众开放，任由任何人随意进出。若由我决定，我会彻底封闭通往街道的入口，但女皇根本不肯考虑。水闸更容易防守；若它成为进入高塔的唯一通道，出入往来便会大幅减少。总有一天，会有不该进来的人偷偷潜入，我们也会为此付出代价——记住我的话。保护国家元首时，再多的安全措施也不算过分。

女皇也不赞同我部署索科洛夫装置的计划。索科洛夫本人当然对安保毫无兴趣，但他爱慕虚荣，因此热衷于看到自己的发明以任何形式得到应用。他一直在摆弄的这道“光之壁”很有前景。无论如何，我至少成功说服女皇升级了城市警卫官员配备的手枪。

为什么别人似乎毫不在意，我却如此忧虑？如果我稍一合眼，一切是否就会沉入大海？那些粗野之物是否会翻过围墙，以我们的血肉饱腹？我每个月都会数次梦见这一幕。只要我在政事上拥有更多话语权、更多权力，我就能保护所有人。

或许我的确工作得太辛苦了。也许该与某位优雅的女士共进晚餐、畅谈一夜，地点不妨选在豪宅区某个体面的地方。

--希拉姆·巴罗斯，皇家情报部长
reason: 人工裁决: 整体纠错必要，但Estate District是具名城区，应译为“豪宅区”；当前“地产区”误取房地产义。其余内容可保留，因此仅修正该处。

en:
[Excerpt from an Overseer's covert field report]

For over a year now, I have lived away from the Abbey, without the company of my Overseer brethren or the guidance of the blind sisters of the Oracular Order. Days have passed with me sleeping in the dens of cut-purses, murderers and worse, and the nights have seen me prowling through the worst alleys and wretched corners of Dunwall. I have taken my meals with killers. At times I have ventured beyond the city walls, meeting in forgotten graveyards and the outlying ruins frequented by those of ill means. 

My beard has grown long and I wear the weathered clothing and bits of boiled leather favored by the Bottle Street and Hatter gangs, and by those rough men and women who make their trade knifing others in return for coin. My hands have run red with blood, it's true, but I have selected my targets with care, choosing among those criminals and heretics who were not fit to live, executing them justly and using their deaths as a means of building my reputation. So far this trick has allowed me to make my name among my murderous colleagues, without taking the lives of the innocent. 

My goal is singular: I must impress the assassin named Daud in order to get close to him. 

Of all of the practitioners of black magic we have tracked, none concern the Abbey as much as Daud. It is said that his mother was a witch from one of the archipelagos off the Pandyssian coast, taken captive by pirates venturing far from the Isles. According the legend, by the time the ship returned, the captain was dead and the witch controlled the crew, with Daud still a shadow in her belly. 

The earliest stories tell of a gang-killer without mercy, moving among the shop keepers and City Watch officers of Dunwall like a reaper through wheat. Then a period of silence followed; years we now believe he spent traveling the Isles, studying anatomy and the occult in the great halls of learning and in hidden basements frequented by fellow dabblers in the forbidden arts. Daud is even purported to have spent a winter in the Academy of Natural Philosophy itself. And for a time, before a schism developed, he counted the Brigmore Witches among his allies. All the while, he honed his craft, and it is during this time that we believe he began to consort with the Outsider. 

New reports emerged of a dusky-skinned assassin, paid by the elite to eliminate their rivals in Dunwall and in the other major cities across the Isles. Those who saw him and lived numbered in the handful, but all of them reported something strange. He appeared and vanished like smoke. From a nearby rooftop, he gestured and a noble woman stumbled from her balcony, falling to her doom on the cobblestones below. Most recently, as this new threat of plague has risen in Dunwall, Daud has been seen leading a gang of men in dark leather, dressed as factory whalers in their vapor masks. They seem loyal beyond comprehension for one so unworthy, leading me to wonder if some of his magic is dedicated to lulling their minds, enslaving them. 

Only a month ago, one young girl claims to have come upon a strange scene. Carrying a bottle of milk home to her crippled brother, she was taking a shortcut through the Tailors' District. In a narrow street, she passed beneath a window and heard unusual sounds from within. Pushing aside the ratty curtain, the girl saw into an abandoned apartment, used by miscreants for gambling and trading habber weed. An occult shrine had been erected against the far wall, which she recognized from the teachings given by her local Overseer. A man she described as resembling Daud was kneeling before the shrine muttering to an unseen spirit as if in argument. He took a carving, made of pale bone, from the altar before him and the lights all went out in a gush of unclean wind. Quiet as a field mouse, she slipped away, running until she reached her home. 

There can be no doubt. Daud is an agent of the Outsider and must die, for there is no limit to the evil this man might do. This is my solemn oath and the great purpose of my life. Until Daud is a dead and his corruption has been purged from the world, I will continue to move among the depraved, winding my way toward him. I will not drop my guise or don my Overseer's mask again until Daud breathes no more.
old:
[摘自一位督军的秘场报告]

我离开修道院居住已经超过一年了，这期间我既没有其它督军兄弟也没有神谕秩序院姐妹的陪伴。在我睡在小偷、谋杀犯和其它更糟的家伙身边时白昼就那么慢慢流逝过去了，而当夜晚来临时我则在顿沃最糟糕的巷子和讨人厌的角落里悄悄穿行。我和杀人犯们一同用餐。此外时不时的我就穿过城市围墙去冒险，在那些被遗忘的坟场和荒僻的废墟里和那些恶心的家伙打照面。

我的胡子已经长得非常长了，而我的穿着是一件风化了的破衣服，还有些瓶街帮和帽子帮恩惠施舍来的煮过的皮革。那些粗野的男人和女人们做交易的方式就是拿刀捅其它人，依此来换金币。我的手上也早已沾满了鲜血，这是真的，但是我在选择自己的目标时是很小心的。我会在那群罪犯和异教徒中选择那些不适合活下去的家伙，然后通过处决他们建立自己的名望。目前看来这种把戏已经让我有效地在我的那些凶恶的谋杀犯同事间建立起了自己的威名，而同时我也不用杀死无辜的人。

我的目标只有一个：我必须要给那个叫道德的刺客留下深刻的印象，依此来接近他。

在我们追踪的所有黑魔法术士中，没有一个像道德那样引起了修道院如此密切的关注。据说他的母亲是个来自潘迪希恩海岸附近群岛的女巫，她被一群远航的海盗们抓了起来。根据传说所言，当这艘船返回到港口时，船长死掉了，那女巫控制了所有的船员，而那时她腹中已经怀上了道德。

最早的故事说的是有个毫无慈悲之心的帮派杀手自由的来往于顿沃的商店店主和城市警卫之间，如同收割者于于麦地中穿行一般。接下来的一段时间里他销声匿迹了；而过了这么多年现在我们相信他当时是踏上了前往埃勒斯的旅程，在宏伟的学术大厅和隐蔽的地下室里研究解剖学和神秘学，时不时的还有爱好禁忌艺术的半吊子同伴来拜访他。道德甚至声称自己曾在自然科学院里度过了一个冬天。而在教会分裂事件发展之前，他一度曾把布里格莫尔女巫们当做过盟友。而一直以来他都在不断磨练着自己的技艺，我们相信也就是在那段时间里他开始和界外魔有了来往。

新的报告说出现了个肤色黯淡的刺客，他被上流精英们雇佣去干掉那些人的在顿沃乃至遍及整个埃勒斯重要城市埃勒斯的敌人。那些见过他的人最后都是时日无多，但是他们所有人都反映了个很奇怪的事：道德看上去总是来去如烟。他在附近的一个屋顶上做了个手势，随后就有个贵族女人在自己的阳台上蹒跚起来，然后一头摔死在了下面的鹅卵石上。最近，顿沃受到了瘟疫的威胁，而有人看到道德开始领导一个身着暗色皮革的帮派，其成员全都穿的像工厂捕鲸人一样，带着防毒面具。而看起来他们对于那个一名不值的家伙的忠心真是超过了可理解的范围。这让我怀疑他是不是用了自己的什么魔法迷惑了他们的心智，让他们成了他的奴隶。

而就在一个月之前，一个女孩说自己遇到了非常奇怪的景象。她当时正带着把一瓶牛奶回家，要给自己跛脚的兄弟把牛奶带过去。然后她走了条近道穿过了裁缝区。她在走过那狭窄的街道上的一扇窗户时听到里面传来了不寻常的声音。她把破烂的窗帘拉到了一边，然后走进了一座废弃的公寓里面，那里常常是恶棍们赌博并做哈勃大麻交易的地方。由于当地的督军教过，因此她认出了在远处的墙那里的一座神秘的神龛。她描述说有个很像道德的男人当时跪在神龛前，向一个看不见的灵魂低语着，仿佛在吵架。他从面前的神龛那里拿起了一个由苍白的骨头制成的雕刻品，随后就涌起了一阵风，把所有的灯都吹灭了。她吓得如同一只田鼠一般窜了出去，一直跑到了家才停下。

毫无疑问，道德是界外魔的代理人，而且他必须得死，因为这个邪恶的男人什么都干得出来。我庄重地宣誓，杀死他将成为我终生的目标。直到他死去，直到他的腐败从世上彻底消散之前我将继续自己的堕落与扭曲之路以来接近他。在道德停止呼吸之前我绝不会穿上自己的制服，也不会戴上督军的面具。
new:
[摘自一位督军的秘密实地报告]

一年多来，我一直远离修道院生活，身边既没有督军弟兄陪伴，也得不到神谕教团盲眼姐妹的指引。白天，我睡在扒手、杀人犯乃至更加恶劣之人的巢穴里；夜晚，我则潜行于顿沃最肮脏的小巷和最凄惨的角落。我曾与杀手同桌进餐，有时也会走出城墙，在被遗忘的墓地和城外废墟中，与那些心怀不轨之人会面。

我的胡须已经蓄得很长，身上穿着瓶街帮和帽子帮以及那些收钱杀人的粗野男女所偏爱的破旧衣物和几块硬皮甲。我的双手确实沾满鲜血，但我谨慎选择目标，只挑那些不配活着的罪犯和异教徒，将他们正法，并借其死亡建立自己的名声。迄今为止，这一手段让我在凶残的同伴中打响了名号，同时没有夺走任何无辜者的性命。

我的目标只有一个：我必须博得名叫道德的刺客赏识，从而接近他。

在我们追踪过的所有黑魔法施术者中，最令修道院担忧的便是道德。据说他的母亲是潘迪希恩海岸外某座群岛上的女巫，被远离群岛冒险的海盗俘获。传说那艘船归来时，船长已经死亡，女巫控制了全体船员，而道德当时还只是她腹中的一道影子。

最早的故事称他是一名冷酷无情的帮派杀手，穿行于顿沃的店主和城市警卫官员之间，如同死神收割麦田。随后是一段沉寂；如今我们认为，他用那些年周游群岛，在宏伟的学术殿堂以及禁术研究者出没的隐秘地下室里钻研解剖学与神秘学。据说，道德甚至曾在自然科学院度过一个冬天。在双方因分歧决裂以前，他一度将布里格莫尔女巫视为盟友。与此同时，他不断磨炼自己的技艺；我们相信，他正是在此期间开始与界外魔交往。

后来又有报告称，一名肤色黝黑的刺客受权贵雇佣，在顿沃和群岛其他大城市里铲除他们的对手。亲眼见过他并幸存的人寥寥无几，但他们全都提到了一件怪事：他如烟雾般出现又消失。他站在附近的屋顶上做出一个手势，一名贵族女子便从阳台失足跌落，摔死在下方的鹅卵石上。最近，随着瘟疫开始威胁顿沃，有人看见道德带领着一群身穿黑色皮革、头戴蒸气面具、打扮成工厂捕鲸人的男子。对这样一个卑劣之人，他们的忠诚深得不可思议；这使我怀疑，道德是否用某种魔法麻痹并奴役了他们的心智。

就在一个月前，一名小女孩声称自己撞见了一幕怪异景象。她带着一瓶牛奶回家给残疾的兄弟，途中抄近路穿过裁缝区。经过一条窄街的窗下时，她听到里面传出异常声响。女孩拨开破旧窗帘，望进一处被恶徒用来赌博和交易哈勃草的废弃公寓。远处墙边立着一座神秘学祭坛，她从当地督军的教导中认出了它。一名据她描述酷似道德的男子跪在祭坛前，低声与看不见的灵体争辩。他从面前的祭坛上取下一件苍白骨骼制成的雕刻品，一股不洁之风随即涌起，所有灯光骤然熄灭。女孩像田鼠一样悄无声息地溜走，一直跑回家中。

毋庸置疑，道德是界外魔的代理人，必须死去，因为这个男人可能犯下的邪恶没有极限。这是我的庄严誓言，也是我一生的伟大使命。在道德死去、他的腐化从世界上彻底清除以前，我会继续混迹于堕落之徒中，迂回接近他。在道德停止呼吸以前，我绝不会抛弃伪装，也绝不会再次戴上督军的面具。
reason: 人工裁决: 整体重译修复了原文的连续硬错，但两处直接术语应用范围不当：协调结构中的Bottle Street指瓶街帮，不能译成“瓶巷街帮派”；小写普通短语an abandoned apartment应为“废弃公寓”，不应套用其他版本的地点标签“废弃住宅”。

en:
[Excerpt from the ramblings of a street denizen]

Of course I'll tell you, dearie. I won't keep any secrets from you in the end. 

All the dreary days of my life are like the windows of a house. From the kitchen, I can see out into the garden where the leaves and stalks are brown and bug-eaten. You can see a little lump of dirt where something was wrapped in a blanket and laid to rest along the rows of twisting vines. 

The front room looks out into the street, where the neighbors are all setting fire to their homes, barricading themselves inside. Warm and snug, dearie. 

Don't forget about the bedroom, either. It sees into a dreary alley, where hooligans are playing a game with an old man. The first two are hitting him with sticks and the girl with them is kicking at his dry, old ribs. Oh, to have those bones, to boil them in a pot.

No one lives in my house any more, dearie. No one you'd want to meet. 

When I lived there with my husband, we were fine, fine people. Vera Moray, everyone would say, your house is as grand as Boyle Manor. Better even. Your dinners are lavish and your parties are the best. 

When that young Sokolov came to paint my portrait I was nearly still in my prime. Radiant, he said, and he was just barely a man, so young, painting all the best people across the land. Everyone wanted a portrait by his hand, all my friends. I was the only one, dearie, wet with his paint, glistening on the canvas for a pretty coin.

But it wasn't all parties and paintings. My husband and I weren't always at home, no. We traveled together, he and I, to the far ends of the Isles. Beyond even, all the way to the red cliffs of Pandyssia, to dig in the rock and crawl through the caves, holding up candles and squinting at the walls. Many precious things we came upon, but none so precious as the boy with the black eyes, dearie. All those marks and bones, carved so deep and polished so bright.

I brought the old bones home. Hid them from my dear husband. Then I learned to boil them and carve them myself. They made such good presents, dearie. The little mute boy took them home. He loved them so. All the time he came back with new bones for me, holding them up so I could see it in his eyes, even though his tongue was still. Granny, his eyes would say to me, carve these bones for me. Make me another present. And he went so far, so far, all the way to Dunwall Tower, the Royal Headsman himself now. My little mute boy and his shiny, shiny sword. 

Better bones were what I needed, you see. Better bones to carve and polish, scrape and gleam. My dear old husband was always tired. I made him soup and then he was sick. Better bones, was all. For my little mute boy, carved in the name of the one with black eyes. And after my husband was gone, given away as birthday gifts, I didn't want to live there any more. 

So now I'm old and don't have many to give my presents to. It's sifting through the garbage for Granny Rags, and feeding the little birdies that gather at my feet. No one wants to have tea, dearie. Especially those rude louts on Bottle Street. Slackjaw and his boys, always meddling with an old woman just trying to make her way. 

In the end we'll be together with him. You and me in the dreary night with stars above and below. And always the one with the black eyes, dearie.
old:
[摘自一个街道居民的随笔]

我当然会告诉你啦，可爱的小宝贝。即使是最后我也不会对你保持任何秘密的。

我生命中所有的枯燥的日子宛如屋子的窗户。从厨房那儿，我能看到花园的叶和茎，那些棕黄色和有虫子咬的地方。你可以在被毯子卷起的地方看到一小块污渍，沿着一排排扭藤蔓躺下休息。

前面的房间能看到街道，那里邻居们都在点火烧毁他们的房子，把自己围在里面。温暖而舒适，亲爱的。

同样的，别忘了卧室。它将变成一个沉闷的小巷，那里流氓将和一个老男人玩个游戏。起初的两个人用棍子打他，和他们一起的女孩则是踢在他那干枯，衰老的肋骨。哦，那些骨头，将其煮在锅里。

再没有人住在我的屋子里了，亲爱的。没有你想要见到的人。

当我丈夫和我住在这儿的时候我们是善良的，大好人。每个人会说，维拉莫雷，你的房子是有如波义耳宅邸的宏伟。甚至更好。你的晚餐是奢华的，你的聚会是最好的。

当年轻的索洛科夫来画我的肖像时我几乎仍然在我最好的时光。容光焕发的，他说，他只是一个人，这么年轻，只画这片大陆上所有最棒的人。每个人都想要一幅出自他之手的肖像画。而我是唯一的那个，亲爱的，他的油画还湿着，在画布上闪闪发光，是一个漂亮的金币。

但那不是全部的聚会和画作。我丈夫和我并不总是在家，不是的。我们一起旅行，他和我，去向遥远的群岛的尽头。甚至超越这，一直到潘德萨尔的红色峭壁，在岩石上挖洞，爬出洞穴，举着蜡烛，观察墙壁。许多珍贵的东西我们可以得到，但是没有一件比得上那个黑眼睛的男孩，亲爱的 。所有这些标记和骨头，雕刻的如此之深，抛光得如此明亮。

我把古老的骨头带回了家。从我亲爱的丈夫那儿藏起来。然后我学会了煮它们和自己雕刻它们。她们被制成了如此好的礼物，亲爱的。小哑巴男孩把它们带回家。他如此爱它们。每次他回来都会带给我新的骨头，将它们举起来以至于我可以从他眼中看到那些 ，即使他的舌头还是原状 。老奶奶，他的眼睛在对我说话，为我雕刻这些骨头。令我变成了另一个人。之后他走得如此之远，如此之远，他走向了顿沃塔，现在将自己变成了皇家刽子手。我那小哑巴男孩和他的闪亮，闪亮的剑。

我所需的是更好的骨头，你看到了。更好的骨头来雕刻和打磨，刮磨和闪耀。我那亲爱的年老的丈夫一直很累。我给他喝汤然后他生病了。更好的骨头，是我的全部了。为了我的小哑巴男孩，拥有黑色眼睛的他的名义来雕刻。在我丈夫走了之后，作为礼物分发它们，我再也不愿意住在这里了。

所以现在我老了，我没有很多可以送人的礼物了。这是拉格斯奶奶的经过删选的垃圾，喂那些聚集在我脚边的小鸟。没有人想要喝茶，亲爱的。尤其是那些粗鲁笨拙的住在瓶街的人。大嘴巴和他的男孩们，总是干涉一个只是想要过自己日子的老女人。

最终我们都将和他在一起的。你和我在上下都有星辰的沉闷的夜晚。和那个总是有着黑色眼睛的人，亲爱的。
new:
[摘自一名街头居民的胡言乱语]

我当然会告诉你，亲爱的。到最后，我不会对你隐瞒任何秘密。

我一生中所有阴郁的日子，就像一栋房子的窗户。从厨房望出去，我能看见花园，里面的叶子和茎秆都已变成褐色，被虫子啃噬。扭曲藤蔓排列成行，旁边有一小堆泥土，下面埋着某个曾被毯子包裹、就此安息的东西。

前厅的窗户望向街道，邻居们都在放火烧自己的房子，把自己封死在里面。温暖又舒适，亲爱的。

也别忘了卧室。它望向一条阴郁的小巷，几个流氓正在和一位老人玩游戏。前两个用棍子殴打他，同行的女孩则踢着他干枯衰老的肋骨。哦，要是能得到那些骨头，把它们放进锅里煮该多好。

我的房子里已经没人居住了，亲爱的。至少没有你想见的人。

我和丈夫住在那里时，我们可是非常非常体面的人。大家都会说：维拉·莫雷，你的房子像波义耳庄园一样宏伟，甚至更加气派。你的晚宴奢华无比，你的聚会也最为精彩。

年轻的索科洛夫来为我画像时，我还几乎处在盛年。他说我光彩照人，而他那时也才刚刚成年，如此年轻，却已在为全国最出色的人物作画。我的所有朋友都想得到一幅出自他手的肖像。只有我，亲爱的，只花一笔可观的钱，便能沐浴在他的颜料中，在画布上闪闪发亮。

但生活中并非只有聚会和绘画。我和丈夫并不总待在家里，不。我们一同旅行，他和我，走到群岛最遥远的尽头，甚至越过那里，一直抵达潘迪希恩的红色峭壁。我们挖掘岩石、爬过洞穴，举起蜡烛，眯眼端详墙壁。我们发现了许多珍贵之物，但没有任何东西比得上那个黑眼睛的男孩，亲爱的。还有那些符号和骨头，刻得那么深，磨得那么亮。

我把古老的骨头带回家，瞒着我亲爱的丈夫。后来我学会了如何煮制它们，亲手雕刻它们。它们是那么好的礼物，亲爱的。那个哑巴小男孩把它们带回家，他喜欢极了。他总是带着新的骨头回来，高高举起；即使他的舌头沉默不语，我仍能从他眼中读懂一切。“奶奶，”他的眼睛这样对我说，“替我雕刻这些骨头，再给我做一件礼物。”后来他走了那么远，那么远，一直走到顿沃高塔，如今成了皇家刽子手。我的哑巴小男孩，还有他那闪亮、闪亮的剑。

我需要的是更好的骨头，你明白吗？更好的骨头，可以雕刻、抛光、刮削，让它们闪闪发亮。我亲爱的老丈夫总是疲惫不堪。我给他煮了汤，随后他便病倒了。只是为了更好的骨头。为我的哑巴小男孩，以黑眼睛之人的名义雕刻。丈夫离去后，他的骨头被制成生日礼物送了出去，我也不愿再住在那里。

所以如今我老了，没有多少人可以收下我的礼物。拉格斯奶奶只能翻找垃圾，喂养聚在脚边的小鸟。没人愿意来喝茶，亲爱的，尤其是瓶巷街上那些粗鲁的恶棍。大嘴巴和他的手下总来为难一个只想勉强度日的老妇人。

最终，我们会和他团聚。你和我置身于阴郁的夜晚，头顶和脚下都是星辰。还有那个永远黑着眼睛的人，亲爱的。
reason: 人工裁决: 原译对埋葬土堆、画像、骨头礼物及丈夫结局等内容存在大量实质错译，整体修订必要；当前人物、地点及普通称谓的处理均符合各自语境。

en:
[Excerpt from a theatre play]

Young Lady Amelia, in the back garden
Duchess, I do not know of the world beyond these garden walls, but do not mistake my lack of experience for fear. Or for an absence of desire. If I've avoided you it is because of the warning your name carries. 

Duchess Kalli, bending a rose to her face, inhaling the scent
And what warning is that, my dear Amelia?

Young Lady Amelia, turning her back on the Duchess
I believe you know my meaning. Your father's tales are still the subject of parlor gossip. 

Duchess Kalli, stepping up close 
And do those stories excite you? Tell me, girl, I am a friend.

Young Lady Amelia, hesitating
Duchess Kalli, I - Yes, I confess they do. In my youth I hid a copy of the tales of Prince Kallisarr. I read them late into the night. 

Duchess Kalli, speaking into her ear
As did I. 

Young Lady Amelia, leaning back into her embrace
But, he was your father?! 

Duchess Kalli, stroking her neck
They're just stories, Amelia. Fire for the imagination.

Young Lady Amelia, breathing deeply
Duchess, will you teach me to kiss?

Duchess Kalli, cooing softly
I will, but have you never kissed another?

Abirri, a rose gardner, emerging from the hedges, stammering
My ladies! I swear to you, I did not intend to spy. Forgive me, but I was pruning the hedge and could not find a way to interrupt.

Duchess Kalli, extending a hand
We forgive you. But as punishment, I command you to stay, and to come closer. 

Young Lady Amelia, shocked, brows furrowed in irritation
But he is a servant, Duchess!

Duchess Kalli, pulling at each of them, drawing them close to her
And serve us, he will, young Amelia.
old:
[摘自一部舞台剧]

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，在后院
公爵夫人，我不知道这花园高墙背后的世界，但别将我的缺乏经验误以为是害怕。或是我没有了解的欲望。如果我躲避你那是因为你名字带自的警告。

卡莉公爵夫人，将一朵玫瑰凑近她的脸，吸入香气
而警告是，阿米莉亚？

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，她转身背对公爵夫人
我相信你知道我什么意思。你父亲的故事仍然是客厅的八卦话题。

卡莉公爵夫人，靠近了 
这些故事有使你不安吗？告诉我，女孩，我是你的朋友。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，踌躇不决
卡莉公爵夫人，我 -是的，我承认他们做的。我年轻的时候，我藏了一份卡莉萨尔王子的故事。我在深夜读这些故事。

卡莉公爵夫人，在她耳边诉说
就和我做的一样。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，靠在她的怀抱
但是，他是你的父亲？！

卡莉公爵夫人，抚摸着她的脖子
那些只是故事，阿米莉亚。想象出的火。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，深呼吸
公爵夫人，你会教我接吻吗？

卡莉公爵夫人，轻声低语
我会的，但是你从未轻吻过他人吗？

艾比·厄尔瑞，一位玫瑰花种植员工，从篱笆那儿出现，口吃地说
我的女士啊！ 我向你发誓，我不打算偷听。原谅我吧，但我修剪树篱，是无法中断的。

卡莉公爵夫人，伸出手
我们原谅你。但作为一次惩罚，我建议你留下，快过来。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，震惊了，眉头紧锁感到刺激
但他是一个仆人啊，公爵夫人！

卡莉公爵夫人，拉着他们，让他们接近她
来服侍我们，她会的，年轻的阿米莉亚。
new:
[摘自一部舞台剧]

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，在后花园
公爵夫人，我不了解这花园高墙外的世界，但别把我的缺乏经验误当成恐惧，也别以为我毫无欲望。我一直躲着你，是因为你的名字本身便是一种警告。

卡莉公爵夫人，将一朵玫瑰凑近面庞，吸入花香
那是什么警告呢，我亲爱的阿米莉亚？

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，转身背对公爵夫人
我相信你明白我的意思。你父亲的故事至今仍是客厅闲谈的话题。

卡莉公爵夫人，走到她近前
那些故事让你兴奋吗？告诉我，姑娘，我是你的朋友。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，犹豫着
卡莉公爵夫人，我——是的，我承认，的确如此。小时候，我私藏过一本卡莉萨尔王子的故事集，常常读到深夜。

卡莉公爵夫人，在她耳边低语
我也是。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，向后靠进她的怀抱
可是，他是你的父亲啊？！

卡莉公爵夫人，抚摸她的脖颈
那只是故事，阿米莉亚，是点燃想象的火焰。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，深深呼吸
公爵夫人，你愿意教我接吻吗？

卡莉公爵夫人，轻声呢喃
我愿意，不过你从来没有吻过别人吗？

阿比里，一名玫瑰园丁，从树篱中现身，结结巴巴地说
两位女士！我向你们发誓，我绝非有意窥探。请原谅，我当时正在修剪树篱，实在找不到合适的时机打断你们。

卡莉公爵夫人，伸出一只手
我们原谅你。但作为惩罚，我命令你留下，再走近些。

年轻的阿米莉亚小姐，满脸震惊，恼怒地皱起眉头
但他只是个仆人，公爵夫人！

卡莉公爵夫人，拉住两人，将他们拽到自己身边
而他会好好服侍我们的，年轻的阿米莉亚。

en: [Excerpt from a manual on new City Watch procedures]\n\nCommissioned by the Lord Regent in the face of the growing plague crisis, the Dead Counter is a position that will only be given to officers, usually of junior or middle grades. In most matters of edict or curfew enforcement, these officers will defer to the acting officer on-duty. However, any Dead Counter will have command in situations related to the plague and the handling of the dead, including those with late-stage plague symptoms (called "weepers" in common parlance). Starting in the Month of Rain, interested officers may apply for the test and, if accepted, for the two-week training tour. Pay will be administered in coin and rations of elixir, at one and one-half normal pay grade.
old: [摘自一个新的城市看守程序手册]\n\n受到摄政王的委托，在面对蔓延的瘟疫危机时，计死员是一个只给官员的位置，通常是初级或中级等级。在大多数重要的法令或宵禁实施时，这些官员听从值班的代理官。然而，任何计死员在有关鼠疫和处理死的情况下将获得命令，包括那些有后期鼠疫的症状 (一般被称为 “恸哭者”)。从降雨之月开始，感兴趣的人员可以申请测试，如果被接受，将有为期两周的培训旅游。报酬将是金币和定额管理的药剂，在一个和一个半正常工资等级之间。
new: [摘自一本介绍城市警卫新规程的手册]\n\n面对日益严重的瘟疫危机，摄政王下令设立计死员一职。该职位仅授予城市警卫官员，通常由初级或中级官员担任。在执行大多数法令或宵禁事务时，这些官员应听从当值指挥官。然而，凡涉及瘟疫及死者处理的情况，任何计死员均拥有指挥权，其中也包括呈现瘟疫晚期症状的人，也就是俗称的“恸哭者”。自降雨之月起，有意者可以申请参加考试；通过后，还须接受为期两周的轮训。薪酬将以钱币及药剂配给发放，标准为正常职级薪酬的一倍半。
reason: 人工裁决: 当前译文准确说明计死员的任职范围、瘟疫事务指挥权、两周轮训及一倍半薪酬，修复了原译“培训旅游”和薪酬范围等硬错。

en:
[Excerpt from a longer work, translated from old Serkonan - By Anisa Mateo of Serkonos]

She was shy in the Month of Hearths
Hiding from my scented letters
A sun-dappled cure for my loneliness

She was smiling in the Month of Rain
Eating figs straight from the tree
A dream of sailing around the Isles

She was wed in the Month of Clans
To her sailor cousin from Cullero
A shrill bird, drilling at my chest

She was dying in the Month of Songs
Struck by a disease from the East
A terrible kiss on her distant lips
old:
[摘自一份"更长的工作"，来自古老瑟科诺斯的转变 - 由阿妮萨·圣马特奥，瑟科诺斯]

她在炉火之月里十分害羞
躲避我那散发着香味的信件
一片斑驳治愈了我的孤独

她在降雨之月微笑
直接从树上吃无花果
一份在群岛旁航海的梦想

她在祭祀之月结婚了
和她来自克拉罗尔的水手侄子
有一只尖锐的小鸟，往我的胸口钻

她在欢歌之月快死了
被一种来自东方的疾病袭击了
那是一个可怕的吻，在她那遥远的嘴唇

她在炉火之月羞涩腼腆
躲避我芬芳的信笺
洒满阳光，治愈我的孤单

她在降雨之月笑靥绽放
从树上直接摘食无花果

她在宗族之月嫁作人妇

en:
[Excerpt from a pamphlet on new government sanctioned practices - by Barrister Arnold Timsh]

It is an unfortunate reality that the plague has spread, unchecked, across the city of Dunwall. Of those who are afflicted, very few survive. Many times, when the plague strikes a family, it leaves none in its wake, ending husband, wife, child and elder alike. When this occurs, the homes and businesses of the deceased are left abandoned, a breeding ground for rats, or for illicit trade such as gambling, prostitution or gang activity. The City of Dunwall, with the full blessing of the Lord Regent himself, had no choice but to institute its current policy of seizure. Any property owned by those unlucky citizens brought down by the plague immediately becomes property of the state. The officers of the City Watch, led by the Dead Counters, ensure that these laws are enforced fairly and without corruption.
old:
[摘自一本新政府颁布的惩戒措施册 - 大律师阿诺德·提姆士所写]

事实真是遗憾，瘟疫已经在顿沃不受控制的四处传播开来。那些饱受折磨得人里很少有活下来的。很多时候，当瘟疫侵袭一个家庭时，它不会留下能守灵的人，它会以近乎同样的方式了结掉丈夫，妻子，孩子和老人。当这些发生的时候，那些死者的房子和公司就等于是被遗弃了，它们要么成了老鼠的繁殖场，要么就成了像赌博，卖淫或者帮派活动那些非法交易的交易所。顿沃城，现在在摄政王自己的批准下完全没有选择，只能建立起了掠夺的政策。所有那些因瘟疫倒下的不幸居民的财产将马上变为国家财产。那些城市巡警的长官们，在计死员的带领下，会确保这些法律能公平且干净地被实施。

en:
[Excerpt from a series of lectures on natural philosophy - By Piero Joplin]

Of course I have attempted to improve upon Sokolov's designs. Of course! And why not? After all, it is likely that his thinking was influenced in some small way by our time together at the Academy. We are all part of a community, striving to unknot the mysteries of the Cosmos. Even those among us who possess the greatest minds are often led to a fruitful line of consideration by, how does one say it, our intellectual subordinates. Sokolov is no exception to this, despite the glamor of genius he has cast over the aristocracy.

And further it is true that many of my experiments have failed. No need to gossip about it behind my back in your social clubs and in the very chambers of the Academy itself. Great ambition requires risks. You may laugh now at my Door to Nowhere, but someday you will not. Your children will likely see it as commonly as you see the electric lamps lighting our streets at night. But a few short years ago, you would have laughed at Sokolov's Arc Pylon or Wall of Light. Your laughter, your condescending smiles, they are nothing but evidence of your own limited imagination!

[摘自一系列关于自然科学的讲义 - 皮耶罗·乔普林所写]

我当然试图改进索科洛夫的设计了。当然！干吗不呢？毕竟，他的部分想法很有可能被我们一起在学院工作的那段时光影响了一点点。我们都是团体里的一部分，都试图力求揭开宇宙的奥秘。即使是我们之中那些有着最卓越的头脑的人也常常被带到那些硕果累累的想法上去，那些，话怎么说的来着，我们聪明的下级们的想法上去。尽管索科洛夫的天才在上层社会里熠熠生辉，但是这事对他也没有例外。

进一步说，确实我有不少实验都失败了。但不用在我背后你们那个社交圈里甚至是在学院的议事厅里嘀嘀咕咕散播流言蜚语。伟大的雄心需要承担风险。你们现在也许可以嘲笑我有心无门，但是总有一天你们就笑不出来了。你们的孩子们看待这些会像你们晚上看咱们街边的路灯一样平常。但是就在没几年之前，你们也嘲笑过索科洛夫的电弧塔和光之壁。你们的笑声，你们高傲的笑容，现在它们除了证明你们缺乏想象力以外什么都不是！

我当然试图改进索科洛夫的设计了。当然！干吗不呢？毕竟，他的想法很可能在某种程度上受到了我们共处学院那段时光的影响。我们都是这个团体的一部分，都努力解开宇宙的奥秘。即使是我们之中那些有着最卓越头脑的人，也常常会被——话怎么说来着——才智不如自己的人引向富有成果的思路。尽管索科洛夫用天才的光环迷住了贵族阶层，但这事对他也不例外。

而且，我的许多实验确实失败了。没必要在我背后、在你们的社交圈里，甚至在学院的议事厅里议论纷纷。伟大的雄心需要承担风险。你们现在也许会嘲笑我的“无处之门”，但总有一天你们不会再笑。你们的孩子很可能会像你们看到夜晚点亮街道的电灯一样，习以为常地看到它。然而就在短短几年前，你们本来也会嘲笑索科洛夫的电弧塔或光之壁。你们的笑声和居高临下的微笑，只不过是你们自身想象力有限的证据！

en:
[Excerpt from an Overseer's findings - By High Overseer Tynan Wallace]

Spending two years in the company of heretics, the insane, and those rare, black-hearted villains who were truly practitioners of magic, I can say with truth that I have seen such things as to break the minds of most. While the trials and burnings weigh heavily upon my heart, I must chronicle what has been a unique opportunity to witness the multifarious perversions that the Outsider bestows upon those who seek his black council.

Many of those we faced were accused of bewitching their neighbors or family, controlling them from afar, or even walking around in their skins. And I have seen this with my own eyes, as one woman slid into the form of another, prowling unseen until a vigilant Overseer struck down both the witch and her host. 

Others, detailed herein, were found to stand in two places seemingly at once, or to vanish from one place and appear in another. 

Our work was dire, we knew, for if the followers of the Outsider can truly inhabit the skin of another, or move from place to place like the wind, then how can we hope to erect walls to keep him out? It was these trials that first led us to investigate barriers beyond the physical.

[摘自一位督军的裁决书 - 至高督军泰南·华莱士所写]

花了两年时间和那帮异教徒呆在一起，那帮疯子，那帮少见的，黑心肠的混球们，他们真的会魔法，我得说我见到的这些事能让大多数人发疯。尽管那些审判和火刑对我来说很沉重，但我必须记录下那种特别的机会，那种可以目击那些形形色色的被界外魔诱惑而去追寻他的黑暗团体的人的机会。

我们面对过的许多人都被指控对自己的邻居或者家人实施了巫术以从远处控制他们，甚至是附身他们的皮囊上到处走。我就亲眼见过这样的事，一个女人滑到了另一具躯体里，小心翼翼的潜行，直到一位警觉的督军杀死了这个女巫和她的宿体。

其中还详细地说道，其他的情况还有一个人似乎同时位于两个地方，要么就是从那个一个地方消失又出现在了另一个地方。

我们的工作很可怕，我们知道，因为如果那些界外魔的追随者真的能意念占据其他人的身体，或者像风一样从一个地方移动到另一个地方的话，那我们怎么才能建起能有效把他赶出去的墙呢？而开始带领我们调查那些超越自然的屏障的就是这些审判。

我与异教徒、疯子，以及那些真正施展魔法、罕见而黑心的恶徒相处了两年，可以坦言，我所见之事足以击垮大多数人的心智。尽管审判和火刑沉重地压在我的心头，我仍必须记录下这个绝无仅有的机会：亲眼见证界外魔向那些寻求其黑暗指引之人赐予的种种邪恶异变。

我们遇到的许多人被控蛊惑自己的邻居或家人，从远处控制他们，甚至披着他们的皮囊四处行走。我曾亲眼见过这一幕：一名女子滑入另一个人的躯体，藏匿其中悄然潜行，直到一名警觉的督军同时击倒女巫和她的宿主。

本文还记载了其他案例：有人看似同时站在两个地方，也有人从一处消失，又出现在另一处。

我们知道自己的工作事关重大，因为如果界外魔的追随者真能寄居于他人的皮囊，或像风一样在各处穿行，我们又如何指望筑起围墙阻挡他？正是这些审判，最初促使我们调查超越实体的屏障。

en:
[Excerpt from a volume on the geography and culture of Gristol]

Known for its rolling green hills and foggy meadows, Gristol is the largest of the Isles and is home to half the population of the known world. While most are simple people living in rural areas where sheep, blood oxen and gazelle are raised for their hides and meat, there are also five major cities spread out across the nation. Notably, the capital city of Dunwall is located at the southern end of Gristol. 

In general, the people of Gristol are a merry, hard-working lot, fond of fish dishes, sheep pies and beer. The Abbey of the Everyman has a strong presence in Gristol, with the faithful congregating weekly and for all significant religious holidays. The Imperial Navy, while made up of men from across the Isles, is well regarded in Gristol, where some families hold to the tradition of enlisting at least one boy from each generation, back for long years. 

In addition to farming, shipping and the whaling trade, there are several large mines scattered across Gristol, each controlled by one of the more established aristocratic families, such as the Boyles, Pendletons, or Brimsleys.

格里斯托，不仅以起伏连绵的绿色丘陵和雾蒙蒙的草地而闻名，同时也是埃勒斯最大的岛屿及这个世界里一半人口的家园。这里的大多数人都住在农村，为了皮和肉而饲养绵羊，血牛及瞪羚，民风纯朴。尽管如此，这里同样分布有贯穿国家的五个主要城市。尤其值得一提的是，首都城市顿沃就座落在格里斯托的最南端。

一般来讲，格里斯托人生性快活，勤奋有加。他们喜爱鱼类佳肴，羊肉馅饼和啤酒。因为每周和所有重大的宗教节日时都会举办信仰集会的缘故，修道院在格里斯托的的地位很重要。而帝国海军，尽管其成员来自埃勒斯各处，但它仍然在格里斯托备受尊崇，这使得许多家庭仍保持着每代至少送一个男孩去海军参军多很年再让他们回家的传统。

除了农业，航运业及捕鲸贸易以外，格里斯托还布及有几个大型的矿区，每个矿区都由年代久远的贵族家族掌控，如波义耳家族，潘德顿家族及布里姆斯利家族。

en:
[Excerpt from a recent historical work on Kingsparrow Island]

Kingsparrow Island sits in the middle of the Wrenhaven River, and up through the previous century, it was only used by fishermen and for occasional religious ceremonies. 

During the time of the Morley Insurrection, a fort and naval dock were added to the island, as a means of protecting the city from attacks by sea.

In the time of the Rat Plague Crisis, shortly after the tragic death of Empress Jessamine Kaldwin, Dunwall's acting Regent Hiram Burrows commissioned the construction of a modernized military installation and lighthouse on the island. 

Burrows Lighthouse, only recently completed, is widely considered to be one of the marvels of the modern age, humming with Sokolov's technologies, powered by processed whale oil.

[Excerpt from a letter found in an empty house at the edge of the Rudshore Financial District]

The looting started in the warehouses. Once enough men took sick with the plague, the companies had to suspend operations.

My husband Malkus was with the Meierson Tobacco Leaf Company, which closed last year during the Month of Clans. He ran the fire boxes at the main curing barn. Malkus always said flue curing made the sweetest leaf. Sickness hits the tobacco men hardest because of all the smoking.

They ran with a small crew for a while, but around the time my husband got sick the fires were put out and the tobacco sat rotting. 

Somehow the thieves knew and started stripping the place. Later, they moved on to houses, the bastards.

en:
[Excerpt from a volume on Morley geography and culture]

It's said that the history of Morley is as colorful as a quilt made from all the flags ever flown and all the clothes ever worn. The land itself hides from the sun under a layer of clouds, and thick gray moss hangs from the trees, but the spirit of the people who live in Morley dances like the firelight. 

Among the people, the love of good food and drink is legendary, with stews and roasted meat dishes most often used to fight off the cold and the dreariness. The nation has a rich tradition of poets, musicians and philosophers, even among the poorest folk. Intellectual tomes and bar songs alike were often penned in Morley. 

A late entry into the Empire, the Morley Insurrection is still a sore point for many natives, and independence is a proud character trait among the people.

en:
[Excerpt from a book on the Far Continent, Pandyssia]

At the Academy of Natural Philosophy they speak of the Pandyssian Continent as a place of wonder, where all of life has intwined and blossomed across aeons, producing a vibrant ecology unrivaled in the civilized world. The Overseers from the Abbey of the Everyman, by contrast, talk of horror and heresies. Of cults of sub-men engaged in brutal, perverse rituals. 

The few who have traveled to the Far Continent and come back to the Isles, those who have actually touched the soil there, have returned with notes that describe vast deserts, deep jungles, and outlandish creatures that defy belief. 

Once in a generation, a great effort is mounted to build a colony there, in hopes of this someday growing into a port city to rival Dunwall itself. But to date, these attempts have all ended in madness and failure.
old:
[摘自一本关于遥远的大陆潘迪希恩的书]

在学院里科学家们说起潘迪希恩大陆都将之形容为奇迹之地，那里的所有生命已经编织盛开了万古之久，它们制造出了一个生机勃勃的生态坏境，没有文明世界能够与之相比。而相反的，谈到此处修道院的督军们说起的是这里的恐怖和异端邪说，他们说那些非人之人组织的邪教常常计划残忍而堕落的仪式。

极少的那几个在去过这片遥远的大陆后又回到埃勒斯，那几个真正踏上过那片土地的人返回的时候带了笔记。他们的笔记描绘了广阔的沙漠，茂密的丛林，还有那些挑战信仰的奇特生物。

曾经有段时期，人们用了极大的努力试图在那里建立一个殖民地，希望它最终能成长为一座海港城市并和顿沃竞争。但是直到今天，这些尝试最终全部以疯狂和失败告终。
new:
[摘自一本关于遥远大陆潘迪希恩的书]

自然科学院的人谈起潘迪希恩大陆时，会将其描述为一片奇迹之地。那里的万物经过亿万年交织繁衍，孕育出充满生机的生态，文明世界无可比拟。相比之下，众生修道院的督军谈论的却是恐怖与异端，是由亚人邪教举行的残忍而堕落的仪式。

曾经前往遥远大陆又返回群岛的人寥寥无几。那些真正踏上过当地土地的人带回了笔记，其中描绘着广袤沙漠、幽深丛林，以及令人难以置信的奇异生物。

每隔一代人，人们便会倾尽全力尝试在那里建立殖民地，希望它有朝一日成长为足以与顿沃匹敌的港口城市。但直到今天，所有尝试都以疯狂和失败告终。
reason: 人工裁决: 当前译文修正了机构名、群岛指代、once in a generation 及 defy belief 等明确错误；“文明世界”中的“世界”是普通词义，并未误套物品术语。

en:
[Except from a forward-gaffer's journal  - By Old Grum]

These new ships made by that Sokolov fellow make life easier than it was in my youth, I'll tell you what. Ere was, we were at the mercy of the winds. Nowaday, the engines git up at first whale-sign and there aint time enow to roust the boys from they're bunks afore you're on the herd.

We cull out the biggest bastard we can lay eyes on and the pilots drag us out from the circlin' brutes. Them things groan and bellow across the water, like they're callin' to each other. Men below say you can feel it in the hull.

But when the harpoons go in, the beast cannot make for deep water no more. Once it weaks from lost blood, we launch the hook-boat and put chains into the tail. Then the winches drag the bastard backward up the chute and into the rigging overhead.
old:
"[摘自一位导航老人的日志  - 老格鲁姆所写]

我告诉你，多亏了那个叫索科洛夫的家伙造的船，现在捕鲸比我年轻的时候容易多了。在之前啊，我们完全听风摆布。现在呢, 只要看见鲸鱼的影子引擎立马就能运转得飞快, 快得连你从船首回去叫醒那些睡着的水手们的时间都没有.

我们要捕杀的是看到的最大的鲸鱼，领航员会带领我们甩开在船周围盘旋的那些。鲸鱼游来游去，呻吟着，叫唤着，就像在互相召唤同伴，船舱下面的伙伴们说，整个船身都能感到这些大家伙们带来的震动。

但是当鱼叉刺中它们的时候，这些畜生就回不到深水里去了。等到它失血过多，变得虚弱时，我们就让钩船下水，把铁链钩进鲸鱼的尾巴，之后绞车就把这畜生向后拖到斜槽上，最后吊在吊索上。
new:
[摘自一名前甲板捕鲸工头的日志——老格鲁姆所著]

我跟你说，索科洛夫那家伙造的新船，让如今的日子比我年轻时轻松多了。过去，我们完全受风摆布。现在只要发现鲸鱼的踪迹，引擎立刻发动；还没来得及把小伙子们从铺位上叫起来，船就已经追上鲸群了。

我们会挑出能看见的最大一头畜生，领航员则拖着我们离开那些盘旋的巨兽。它们的呻吟与吼叫横越水面，仿佛在彼此呼唤。下面的人说，隔着船体都能感受到那声音。

可一旦鱼叉刺进去，那畜生就再也逃不到深水里。等它因失血变得虚弱，我们便放下钩船，把铁链钩进它的尾巴。随后绞盘将那畜生倒拖上斜槽，送进头顶的索具。
reason: 人工裁决: 裁决证据明确表明 forward-gaffer 是捕鲸岗位；“船首帆工”仍属实物职务误译，应最小修正为“前甲板捕鲸工头”。

en:
[Excerpt from a hound trainer's guide]

From each litter, there's usually somewhere shy of four good pups, but we always drown the runt. 

Them that remain spend three or so months sucklin' from their mothers before we start 'em up with the training. It's simple at first, returning sticks and sitting still on command. Only pissin' outside and the like. But by the eighth month, we got 'em hunting for scented sack-dolls hidden in a scrub forest, killin' wild pigs on command, and taking a man in padded armor down by hangin' onto his forearm.  

At the end of the first year, we graduate the ones that've learned and shoot the ones that haven't. The Overseers take them after that and we never see them again. 

Except once. Walking down Clavering Boulevard, an Overseer passed me, preachin' about the Litany on the White Cliff and the evils of witchery, and sure enough his hound started whimpering and waggin' its tail. That's how I knew it was one of mine, whelped up from a pup.
old:
[摘自一本猎犬训练者的指南]

每一窝里我们总有需要四只好狗，然而数量总是不够。但我们总是淹死那些没发育好的。

剩下的那些会由它们的母亲喂养三个月左右，然后我们就开始训练它们。开始的训练很简单，就是把棍子叼回来，在命令下坐着不动，还有只在外边尿尿一类的。但是第八个月的时候，我们会训练它们用嗅觉找到灌木丛里的布娃娃，听从命令杀死野猪，以及通过吊在那些穿着加衬护甲的人的前臂上来放倒敌人。 

在第一年年底时，那些学会了的猎犬就可以毕业了，而那些没学会的我们就射杀掉它们。之后督军们会把它们领走，而我们就再也见不着它们了。

只有一次例外。那一次我走在克拉文鹰大道上，一位督军经过我身边，他正在用关于白崖连祷文的布道，而我确信，他的猎犬一边呜咽一边摇着尾巴。这让我知道它是那些我从小带大的狗之一。
new:
[摘自一本猎犬训练者的指南]

每一窝通常能挑出不到四只好幼犬，但最弱小的那只总会被我们淹死。

剩下的幼犬会跟着母犬吃奶三个月左右，然后我们才开始训练。起初很简单：把棍子叼回来、听命令安静坐着，以及只在室外撒尿之类。但到了第八个月，我们就会让它们寻找藏在灌木林里的带气味布袋人偶，听从命令杀死野猪，并咬住穿软甲者的前臂，将其拖倒。

第一年结束时，我们让学会本领的猎犬毕业，射杀那些没学会的。之后督军会将它们带走，我们便再也见不到它们。

只有一次例外。我走在克拉文鹰大道上时，一名督军从身边经过，正在宣讲白崖连祷文以及巫术之邪恶。他的猎犬果然开始呜咽摇尾。我这才认出，那是由我从幼犬养大的一只。
reason: 人工裁决: 原译首句误作“需要四只但数量不够”，且末段漏译“巫术之邪恶”；另将训练动作译为“吊在前臂上”等明显病句。

en:
[Excerpt from notes by Dr. Galvani on proper procedure for handling those infected with plague]

Once a victim bleeds from the eyes, you cannot help them. Death is inevitable, given our current understanding of the plague. However, by following protocol we can limit its spread. 

All personnel handling "weepers", or  those in the final stages, must consume liberal amounts of one of the available protective potions. Any of the variants will serve this purpose: Sokolov's Elixir or Piero's Remedy, for instance. A dose per day for the enlisted men. A dose twice daily for officers. 

Distance must be maintained, either through the use of pole arms or incendiary ranged weapons, in order to avoid the parasitic stinging insects that colonize an infected host. 

After use, strict washing procedures must be followed with regard to washing the metal kennels, transport paddocks, and the carriages used to transport the infected to one of the deportation zones, such as the Flooded District.
old:
[摘自加尔瓦尼医生处理瘟疫感染者的过程记录]

瘟疫受害者出现双眼出血的症状时，你就帮不了他们了。根据我们现有的对这种瘟疫的了解，死亡不可避免。然而，根据现有的报告我们能够阻止它扩散。

所有人在处理那些“恸哭者”，或者那些处于症状末期的病人时，必须大量服用一种保护性药剂。服用任何这种药剂的变体也可以达到效果： 比如索科洛夫生命药剂或者皮耶罗精神药剂。执勤的人者一天一剂，军官一天两次，每次一剂。

必须和他们保持距离，要么用竿型武器要么用燃烧型远程武器，这样才能避开那些寄生在感染者身上会叮人的昆虫。

在出勤之后，必须严格执行那些清洗工作： 清洗金属狗屋，交通围场，还有那些曾被用来把感染者运到像水淹区那样的驱逐区的马车。
new:
[摘自加尔瓦尼医生关于正确处理瘟疫感染者程序的笔记]

瘟疫受害者出现双眼出血的症状时，你就帮不了他们了。根据我们现有的对这种瘟疫的了解，死亡不可避免。然而，只要遵循规程，我们就能限制它的扩散。

所有人在处理那些“恸哭者”，或者那些处于症状末期的病人时，必须大量服用一种保护性药剂。服用任何这种药剂的变体也可以达到效果：比如索科洛夫生命药剂或者皮耶罗精神药剂。士兵一天一剂，军官一天两次，每次一剂。

必须和他们保持距离，要么用长柄武器，要么用燃烧型远程武器，这样才能避开那些寄生在感染者身上、会叮人的昆虫。

使用之后，必须严格执行清洗程序，清洗金属笼舍、运输围场，以及那些曾被用来把感染者运到水淹区等驱逐区的马车。
reason: 人工裁决: 当前译文正确恢复了“遵循规程”、士兵剂量及长柄武器等信息；metal kennels 在此是处理感染者所用的金属笼舍，不是地点名“狗舍”。

en: [Excerpt from lab notes - By Anton Sokolov]\n\nThe bulk of the rodent is hardly the most interesting detail, though it is the one first remarked upon by visiting colleagues who come to study my prize from Pandyssia. Upon further observation, it becomes obvious that the specimen exhibits greater cunning than its cousins native to temperate Gristol. Twice in the night I have awoken to find it loose in my apartments, so a new cage had to be devised. An entertaining diversion, but a waste of my precious time. The dietary tests I have conducted have also provided some surprise. The Pandyssian Bull Rat, I can say with confidence, is not a finicky eater. With equal gusto, I have seen my little guest dine upon other, smaller rats, living felines, and even the corpse flesh of a plague-dead woman found in the Wrenhaven River. Further study is required.
old: [摘自实验室笔记 - 安东·索科洛夫所写]\n\n一些来自潘迪希恩同事因我为研究设置的奖励来拜访我。尽管他们都最先注意到了这种啮齿动物的巨大体型，但这难以称得上是其最有趣的特征。进一步的观察很明显地显示出这些样本比它们在温和的格里斯托地区本地生长的表亲们狡猾的多。我在夜里起来了两次，在公寓里寻找这只跑掉的巨鼠，看来我不得不设计新笼子了。很有趣的消遣，但也是对我宝贵时间的浪费。我实施的饮食实验也带来了一些惊喜。我可以自信的说，潘迪希恩巨鼠不是什么挑剔的食客。我看见我的小客人以同样的热情进食着一切，不论是其它小一点的老鼠，活的猫科动物，甚至是我从瑞哈文河里找到的一具因为瘟疫死掉的女尸，都一样热情。看来还需要作进一步的研究才行。
new: [摘自实验室笔记 - 安东·索科洛夫所写]\n\n尽管前来研究我这只潘迪希恩珍贵样本的同事们最先注意到的总是这种啮齿动物的巨大体型，但这难以称得上是其最有趣的特征。进一步观察后，很明显，这个样本比它在气候温和的格里斯托土生土长的表亲们狡猾得多。有两次我夜里醒来，发现它逃出笼子在我的住处乱跑，因此不得不设计一种新笼子。很有趣的消遣，但也是对我宝贵时间的浪费。我实施的饮食实验也带来了一些惊喜。我可以自信地说，潘迪希恩巨鼠不是什么挑剔的食客。我看见我的小客人怀着同样的热情，吃掉其他体型较小的老鼠、活的猫科动物，甚至一具在瑞哈文河中发现的、死于瘟疫的女尸之肉。看来还需要作进一步的研究。
reason: 人工裁决: 原译将 my prize from Pandyssia 错解为同事因“研究奖励”来访，并将夜间醒来发现巨鼠逃脱译成起床寻找；女尸的发现者指代也发生偏移。

en:
[Excerpt from a series of interviews with street workers - By Rat Catcher Lena]

Used to be, you'd go out with a bag, a stick with a nail on the end, and catch as many rats as you could in a night. The City Watch paid by weight. My husband Benjamin and I mostly worked alone, and we got by. If we found a place where the rats were real bad, sometimes we'd hire a crew of street brats to work with us, the younger ones who didn't make trouble. We'd pay them with bread and apple cider.

Once the plague came, the rats were different. Meaner, bigger and a little quicker. You had to watch yourself. If you got cornered, they'd turn and the swarm would come back at you. I barely got away with my skin a few times, down in the sewers. The bites hurt afterward, but it was the sounds they made that stayed in your dreams at night. 

It got more dangerous, and the City Watch started paying better. But that didn't last long because after a while too many people had been stripped clean, trying to fill up a bag. One slip and they'd be all over you, gnawing and trying to chew down to the bone. That's how I lost my poor Benji.
old:
[摘自一系列对街道工人进行的采访 - 捕鼠人蕾娜所写]

以前，你出去的时候背个袋子，带个尾端带钉子的棍子，然后在晚上尽你可能的多抓老鼠。城市警卫会按老鼠的重量付给你钱。我丈夫本杰明和我大多数时候都自己单干，我们的日子还过得去。当我们发现有地方老鼠泛滥成灾时，我们偶尔会雇用那些不会惹麻烦的街头小孩和我们一起干，用面包和苹果酒作为报酬。

而瘟疫一来，老鼠也不一样了。它们变得更狡猾，更大，也比以前更灵活了一些。你自己要小心。如果你被逼到死角里的话，鼠群会回过头来扑向你。有几次在下水道里，我真是死里逃生。它们的噬咬在之后会很疼，但那种发出来的声音才是你晚上最可怕的梦魇。

这件差事变得越来越危险了，城市警卫给的报酬也开始变高了。但这没持续很长时间，因为没多久后有太多的人被剥削的干干净净，他们不得不艰难求生。只要稍微犯个错，他们就会向你一拥而上，折磨你，把你嚼到只剩骨头为止。我就是这样失去了我可怜的本杰。
new:
[摘自一系列对街道工人进行的采访 - 捕鼠人蕾娜所写]

以前，你出去的时候背个袋子，带根末端钉着钉子的棍子，然后一晚上尽可能多抓些老鼠。城市警卫会按老鼠的重量付给你钱。我丈夫本杰明和我大多数时候都自己单干，日子还过得去。当我们发现有地方老鼠泛滥成灾时，偶尔会雇用那些不会惹麻烦的街头小孩和我们一起干，用面包和苹果酒作为报酬。

而瘟疫一来，老鼠也不一样了。它们变得更凶、更大，也比以前更快了一些。你自己要小心。如果你被逼到死角，鼠群就会转身扑向你。有几次在下水道里，我真是死里逃生。被咬的地方之后会很疼，但真正留在你夜间梦里的，是它们发出的声音。

这件差事变得越来越危险，城市警卫给的报酬也开始变高。但这没持续很长时间，因为过了一阵，太多想装满一袋老鼠的人反被啃得干干净净。只要稍有失误，它们就会向你一拥而上，啃咬你，直到咬到骨头。这就是我失去可怜的本杰的经过。
reason: 人工裁决: 当前译文修正了 meaner 的性情含义以及 stripped clean 所指的捕鼠者遭鼠群啃食，动作、因果和报酬对象均准确；“下水道”在此也是自然的普通词义。

[Excerpt from a letter found in an empty house at the edge of the Rudshore Financial District]

The looting started in the warehouses. Once enough men took sick with the plague, the companies had to suspend operations.

My husband Malkus was with the Meierson Tobacco Leaf Company, which closed last year during the Month of Clans. He ran the fire boxes at the main curing barn. Malkus always said flue curing made the sweetest leaf. Sickness hits the tobacco men hardest because of all the smoking. 

They ran with a small crew for a while, but around the time my husband got sick the fires were put out and the tobacco sat rotting. 

Somehow the thieves knew and started stripping the place. Later, they moved on to houses, the bastards.

[摘自一封在赭岸金融区一座空房子里找到的信]

掠夺由仓库开始。一旦染上瘟疫的人足够多了，那些公司就必须暂停运营。

我丈夫马库斯是迈尔森烟草公司的员工，这公司在去年的祭祀之月关闭了。他负责主加工仓的火箱。马库斯总说烟道加工制出的烟叶是最棒的。所有的烟草工人都吸烟，因此疾病对他们的攻击也最厉害。

在一小段时间里他们运营起了一小群员工，但随着时间推移我的丈夫病了，由于火箱的火灭了，因此那些烟草全烂掉了。

那些贼不知道怎么知道了这件事，他们开始搜刮这个地方。不久之后，他们就去搜刮房子了，这群混蛋。

en:
[Excerpt from a volume on Serkonan geography and culture]

Serkonos, the jewel of the South, is best known for its warm winds, spiced foods and endless beaches. While the city of Cullero sees the heaviest flow of travelers from across the Isles, Karnaca, on the Southernmost edge of the known world, is preferered among the elite of the Empire. It is said that a month spent resting beneath the sun on the beaches of Serkonos, or within one of the rural villages, can cure most maladies. Travelers bring back recipes and styles from the South, and the dances that all Serkonans learn in their youth are favored in Gristol for their sensuality, copied by the fashionable aristocracy in the capital city of Dunwall. 

The only persistent trouble in Serkonos originates along the string of tiny islands stretching away from the mainland to the East. For generations, pirates have hidden among this archipelago, raiding traders passing between the Isles and, more recently, attacking whaling ships returning with rich stores of oil.
old:
[摘自一册关于瑟科诺斯地理及文化的卷集]

瑟科诺斯，南方王冠上的宝石，以它和煦的暖风，辣的食物和无垠的沙滩而闻名。尽管库雷罗城迎接来自埃勒斯四面八方的游客最多，但是卡尔纳卡，这个坐落在该地区最南边的城市，则成为了帝国精英们的首选。据说，休息时只要在瑟科诺斯的海滩上晒上一个月的太阳，或者在这里一座乡下村庄中度过这段时间可以治愈大部分疾病。旅行者们不仅带回了南方的风格和食谱，还有所有瑟科诺斯人自年轻时就学习的舞蹈。这种舞蹈在格里斯托因其肉体上的诱惑感而大受欢迎，因而首都顿沃的时髦贵族们也争相学习这种舞蹈。

唯一持续困扰瑟科诺斯的问题源于它东边远离大陆的一串成线的岛链。好几代以来，海盗们藏匿于这些群岛之中，抢劫穿过这里和埃勒斯的商贸船只。而最近以来，他们一直攻击带着丰富油储回港的捕鲸船。
